edits.body_md:
If a man says, "If Allah heals my sickness, or returns to me the one who is absent, or grants me wealth or a child, then I owe such and such a vow," and he names that vow, then he is bound to fulfill it once Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has done for him what he longed for, since he laid the vow upon himself in the matter. But if he does not name the vow, saying only, "If such a thing comes to pass, of what I have mentioned, then I owe a vow to Allah," without specifying what that vow is, then nothing is required of him. If he vowed some particular thing, it suffices him, and it stands as a voluntary act, not an obligation laid upon him. And if he makes his vow after the measure of the expiation of an oath, that is good and seemly.

### Concerning the Expiations

> لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِٱللَّغْوِ فِىٓ أَيْمَنِكُمْ وَلَكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا عَقَّدتُّمُ ٱلْأَيْمَنَ ۖ فَكَفَّرَتُهُۥٓ إِطْعَامُ عَشَرَةِ مَسَكِينَ مِنْ أَوْسَطِ مَا تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ أَوْ كِسْوَتُهُمْ أَوْ تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍۢ

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: "Allah will not take you to task for the thoughtless word in your oaths, but He will take you to task for the oaths you have deliberately sworn. Its expiation is the feeding of ten poor persons from the average of that with which you feed your own families, or the clothing of them, or the freeing of a slave. Whoever does not find the means, then a fast of three days. That is the expiation of your oaths when you have sworn. And guard your oaths. Thus does Allah make clear to you His signs, that you may be grateful" (al-Maidah: 89).

So whoever swears by Allah and then breaks his oath with a breach that makes expiation obligatory upon him owes the expiation set down above. If he is able, he feeds ten poor persons, or clothes them, or frees a slave, and he is free to do whichever of these he wishes, for he has the choice among them.

Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), said: of everything in the Quran stated with "or," giving the choice among options, the one to whom it applies has that choice; but wherever it is stated, "if he does not find" or "if he is not able," then he must perform the first whenever he finds it and is able, and the second does not suffice him until he can neither find the first nor perform it. So if the one who swore can find nothing with which to feed ten poor persons, and has the means neither to free a slave, whether of small worth or great, nor to clothe ten poor persons, then he must fast three days. Fasting does not stand in place of the rest until none of what has been named, neither food, nor clothing, nor manumission, can be found.

> لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِٱللَّغْوِ فِىٓ أَيْمَنِكُمْ وَلَكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا عَقَّدتُّمُ ٱلْأَيْمَنَ ۖ فَكَفَّرَتُهُۥٓ إِطْعَامُ عَشَرَةِ مَسَكِينَ مِنْ أَوْسَطِ مَا تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ أَوْ كِسْوَتُهُمْ أَوْ تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍۢ

The feeding in the expiation of an oath is not discharged by a single day's provision given to the poor; the least of it is a mudd of food, together with what supports it. The middle grade of seasoning, the idam, is vinegar and oil; meat is the highest grade; and salt alone is the lowest, which does not suffice. This rests upon the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, "from the average of that with which you feed your families" (al-Maidah: 89). The average is the most balanced: whatever the one making expiation feeds his household on most of his days and in the general run of his circumstances is what he ought to feed in the expiation of an oath. If he feeds them better than that, it is the more excellent for him.

As for the clothing in the expiation of an oath, each poor person is to receive two garments.

In the expiation of an oath, the freeing of a slave born into bondage suffices. The freeing of a mudabbar slave, one whose release has been tied to his master's death, is not permitted unless the master first revokes that arrangement, the tadbir, returns him to the condition of a slave, and then frees him. The fast in the expiation of an oath is three consecutive days.

The feeding and clothing of the people of allegiance from the expiation of an oath is what is enjoined upon those who are commanded to it. If such persons are not to be found, then those of the weak who harbor no enmity are entitled to it. But one must not give to a Nasib, who is known for his hostility toward the family of Muhammad, (ع), anything from expiation, nor from charity, nor from anything else of the sort, even if no one but him can be found.

Whoever lays a vow upon himself concerning some matter, in case it should come to pass, when in truth it had already come to pass before he bound himself to it, and he had no knowledge that it had occurred, then nothing is required of him. A man questioned Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali about the like of this, saying: "I have a slave girl by whom I am loath to have a child. Her menses ceased to come on time, and I feared that she had conceived, so I bound myself before Allah to free a slave, to fast, and to give charity if she should menstruate. Then she menstruated, but before I had bound myself to all this, and I did not know it." He said: "Nothing is required of you."

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali said: if a man swears that he will not give another man dinars, and then gives him goods in their place, he has not broken his oath. If a man swears that he will not sell his wares at a price he has named, and then sells them for goods worth that same price, he has not broken his oath. And if a man is owed dinars by another and swears that he will not receive them except in full, and is then given part of them in coin and part in goods of equal value, he has not broken his oath.

He, (ع), was asked about a man who swears to slaughter his son, and he said: "There is nothing upon him in that, and it is among the steps of Satan."

And he said: the expiation comes after the breaking of the oath.

edits.chapter_key: the body's portion: food, drink, and healing
edits.body_md:
Turning from oaths to what the body itself takes in, the law marks out clearly what may be eaten and what must be set aside. Among the parts of a slaughtered animal that are not eaten are the male glands, the penis, the female organ, and the inside of the kidneys.

It is narrated from him, (ع), that he said: "Nothing of the creatures of the sea is to be eaten except what is caught alive and has scales. As for what dies in the water before it is taken, or what has no scales, eating it is forbidden."

He forbade eating the cheese made by the Magians and the polytheists when they put into it rennet (al-anfaha) taken from carrion or from an animal over which the name of Allah was not pronounced. But if the cheese is of unknown origin, and it is not known that any such thing is in it, then eating it is permitted when it is sold in the market of the Muslims, just as one may eat the slaughtered meat sold there.

Everything whose eating is forbidden becomes permissible for the one in dire necessity, when he can find nothing else and fears for his life; and the one compelled by need may eat of it until he is satisfied, if he wishes.

Everything that serves as nourishment for man, the grains, the green herbs, what the earth brings forth, and all the fruits that neither harm nor kill, is lawful to eat. The flesh of camels, cattle, sheep, and all wild animals, together with their milk, is lawful, except for the beasts of prey that possess fangs and seize and devour other animals; their flesh, and nothing of them, is lawful to eat. All birds are lawful when slaughtered, except the birds of prey that possess talons and seize and devour other birds; eating them is not lawful, nor is eating their eggs.

If an egg is found and it is not known what creature it is from, it is examined: if its two ends differ, one pointed and one rounded, it is eaten, for that is the egg of a creature whose flesh is eaten; but if its two ends are alike, it is not eaten, for that is the egg of a creature whose flesh is not eaten. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted the eating of the rabbit, but disliked the lizard (al-dabb), the hedgehog, and the other creeping things of the earth.

From Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) it is narrated that he permitted the use of vessels touched by impurity or wine once they have been washed and cleaned; and concerning food in which the small creatures of the earth, flies, and whatever has no blood happen to die, he said that this does not render the food forbidden to eat, nor does it make it impure. Whoever is repelled by it may leave it, and whoever wishes may eat. But if a creature possessing blood dies in it, then if the food is liquid it is spoiled, and if it is solid only what surrounds the dead creature is spoiled; whoever wishes may eat the rest, and there is no harm in it, once what lay around the dead thing has been removed and thrown away.

**On the Etiquette of Drinking**

It has been narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he forbade drinking in one continuous draft and commanded that one drink in sips, that the drinker name Allah at the first sip and praise Him when he has finished, and that he not breathe into the vessel. He should say "Bismillah" when beginning and "Alhamdulillah" when pausing. Ali (ع) said: "I observed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drinking water more than once, and he would breathe three times during the drink, taking the vessel away from his mouth at each breath, saying Bismillah when he began and Alhamdulillah when he paused." Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع) said: "Three breaths in a drink are better than one."

He forbade drinking from the mouth of a waterskin, that is, bending back its opening and drinking directly from it, saying that this fouls it and carries the risk that a creature in the water, unseen by the drinker, might slip down his throat.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to drink both standing and sitting, yet he forbade lapping water straight from a river, a basin, a pond, or the like. When he saw a man doing so, he said to him: "You lap as a beast laps. If you find no vessel, drink from your hand, for it is the best of your vessels."

He also forbade gulping water down, saying: "Suck the water as it is sucked, and do not gulp it down as a burden upon yourself, for that brings on disease of the liver (al-kubad)." Yet he would gulp milk. Ali ibn al-Husayn (ع) was seen gulping milk, and when he was asked, "Will you not take it in sips?" he answered: "Only the people of the Fire take it in sips." When he drank milk he would say: "O Allah, bless us in it and increase us from it." When he drank water he would say: "Praise be to Allah, who has given us fresh, sweet water by His mercy, and has not given us bitter, briny water on account of our sins."

From Jafar ibn Muhammad it is narrated that he forbade drinking, or performing ablution, from the side of the handle (urwa) of the vessel.

**On What Is Permissible to Drink**

It has been narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Water is the master of drinks in this world and the Hereafter." Any naturally occurring water, in which no human labor has any part, is lawful and permitted to drink, provided it is not mixed with impurity and is neither harmful nor injurious. One may likewise drink the milk of every animal whose flesh is lawful to eat. It has been narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said of camel's milk: "It draws from every tree." And he said: "Cow's ghee is a cure, and its milk is medicine." A prophet once complained of a weakness he found in his body, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to him: "The finest meat is that taken with milk; eat them both, for I have placed strength in both of them." And it is said: "Meat and milk are the broth of the prophets." He said: "Honey is a healing." Ali said: "No sick person was ever healed by the like of honey." And he said: "Can any of you not, when he falls ill, ask his wife to give him a dirham or two from her dowry, and buy honey with it, and drink it dissolved in rainwater?"

> وَنَزَّلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ مُّبَرَكًۭا

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says regarding the dowry: ﴿فَإِنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ نَفْسًا فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا﴾, "If they willingly give up to you any part of it, then consume it in satisfaction and ease" (al-Nisa: 4); and He says regarding honey: ﴿فِيهِ شِفَاءٌ لِلنَّاسِ﴾, "In it is healing for people" (al-Nahl: 69); and He says regarding rainwater: ﴿وَنَزَّلْنَا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً مُبَارَكًا﴾, "And We sent down from the sky blessed water" (Qaf: 9).

Water mixed with honey, milk, or anything similar is lawful to drink, as are drinks made from dates, raisins, or other sweeteners, so long as they have not changed. The same holds for everything pressed from grape juice, dates, raisins, or the fruits and herbs that are lawful to eat: drinking such juice is lawful as long as it has not turned, whether taken pure or mixed with water, and selling it, buying it, and benefiting from it are lawful likewise. So too if grape juice is cooked until it thickens without turning; it is lawful to drink, pure or mixed with water, as long as it does not change. It has been narrated of Ali that he used to provide the people with al-tila, which is grape juice boiled until it gains body and, if left, does not turn but becomes like honey; that and its like are lawful to drink, pure or mixed with water, as long as they do not change. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali was asked about drinking pressed juice, and he said: "There is no harm in it. Drink from a clean vessel that is not seasoned with wine; drink it as long as a large quantity does not intoxicate. But if a large quantity intoxicates, then a small quantity of it is forbidden. Do not drink what has stood a long while, for after an hour, or after a night, the pleasure of wine departs and only its sin remains. So fear Allah and call yourselves to account."

It was the mark of the Shia of Ali that they were known for piety, diligence, restraint, the shunning of sins great and small, and love for the friends of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. It has been narrated from Ali that he said: "We used to soak raisins or dates in water in a clean vessel for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He would drink it that day and the next; and if it had changed by the third day, he ordered it poured away." This is the lawful drink that is called nabidh only because of what is cast, that is, thrown, into the water, of dates, raisins, or the like, which sweetens it when the water is brackish. But if it is left to ferment, so that it boils, intensifies, and throws up froth, then it is wine, and a large quantity of it is forbidden once it intoxicates.

**On What Is Forbidden to Drink**

> يَٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوٓا۟

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّمَا الْخَمْرُ وَالْمَيْسِرُ وَالْأَنْصَابُ وَالْأَزْلَامُ رِجْسٌ مِنْ عَمَلِ الشَّيْطَانِ فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾, "O you who believe, intoxicants, gambling, stone altars, and divining arrows are but an abomination of Satan's handiwork, so avoid it, that you may be successful" (al-Maidah: 90). By this He forbade wine, just as He forbade all things unlawful.

It has been narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Wine is forbidden; no one drinks it in this world and then drinks it in the Hereafter, in the sacred enclosure of holiness (hazirat al-quds)." And he said: "Allah has cursed wine: its presser, the one who has it pressed, its seller, its buyer, its drinker, the one who serves it, the one who consumes its price, the one who carries it, and the one to whom it is carried." He said: "That which intoxicates in large quantity is forbidden even in a small quantity." He forbade treating illness with wine and intoxicants, and forbade that they be given to children or animals, saying that the sin falls upon whoever gives it to them.

It has been narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn that he said: "Intoxicating drink comes from five things: dates, raisins, wheat, barley, and honey, that is, besides grapes." And from Muhammad ibn Ali, and upon his forefathers be peace, it is narrated: "The one addicted to wine will meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, on the day he meets Him as one who worships an idol; and whoever drinks a single draft of it, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will not accept a prayer from him for forty nights."

From Jafar ibn Muhammad it is narrated that he said: "Paradise is forbidden to three: the one addicted to wine, the worshipper of idols, and the enemy of the family of Muhammad." From Ali it is narrated: "Whoever drinks wine and dies within forty days of having drunk it meets Allah, Blessed and Exalted, as one who worships an idol." And he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade every intoxicant from every drink, and whatever the Messenger of Allah has forbidden, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden. Every intoxicant is forbidden, and that which intoxicates in large quantity is forbidden even in a small quantity."

A man from the people of Kufa said to him: "May Allah set you right; the jurists of our land say that only wine made from grapes is forbidden." He said to him: "O Sheikh, I do not know what the jurists of your land say. My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: That which intoxicates in large quantity is forbidden even in a small quantity." Jafar ibn Muhammad then said: "Taqiyya is my religion and the religion of my forefathers in everything except three matters: the prohibition of intoxicants, the removing of the two leather socks at ablution, and the saying aloud of Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim, meaning that it be recited aloud in the prayer."

Jafar ibn Muhammad said: "One must not treat illness with wine or intoxicants, nor may women use such a thing to dress their hair, for my father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, that Ali said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has placed no cure in any impurity that He has forbidden." He was also asked about drinking al-fuqqa, and when the questioner had described its nature, he said: "It is forbidden; do not drink it." And he said, concerning the seasoned vessels, that wine was not forbidden on account of such vessels, but that he had forbidden the intoxicant in little and in much alike; he only disliked the seasoned vessels because they alter the drinks.

**On What Makes Medicine Beneficial**

In this chapter we set down what has come from the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), concerning medicine, the treatment and remedy permitted with it, and what they forbade in that regard, all of which falls within the gates of the lawful and the unlawful. It may be that one who doubts what has come from them will deny it when he hears it; and if he uses it without true belief, he will find no benefit in it and so cast it aside. For Allah, Blessed and Exalted, brings benefit through it only to the people who affirm them and submit to their command, who receive what has come from them with acceptance, not to one who takes it as a mere trial, without belief, without intention, and without conviction.

What confirms this is the report narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad: Muhammad ibn Khalid, the governor of Medina, was recovering from an illness that had befallen him, and complained, in a gathering of people, of a pain he felt in his abdomen. Jafar ibn Muhammad said to him: "Shall I not tell you a hadith my father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Abu Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn told me, from his father, from his grandfather that a man complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of a pain he felt in his abdomen. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: Take a drink of honey and cast into it three grains of black seed (shuniz), or five, or seven, and you will be cured by the leave of Allah. He did so and was cured. So take this yourself."

A man of Medina who was present in the gathering objected and said: "O Abu Abd Allah, the hadith is sound, and we have heard it, but we tried it and gained no benefit from it." At this Abu Abd Allah (ع) grew very angry and said: "Allah brings benefit through this only to those who believe in Him and affirm His Messenger (ع), the Muslims who submit to his command and receive it from him with acceptance. As for the hypocrites who doubt it and do not affirm him, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will not benefit them by it. Perhaps you are a hypocrite, and you took it without affirming the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and so you were denied its benefit." The man fell silent, was overcome with shame, and bowed his head, and all who were present in the gathering affirmed the truth of Abu Abd Allah's words. We, for our part, cannot reckon how much of this we have used with sincere intention and certainty and have indeed benefited from it. So whoever turns to anything mentioned in the chapters of this section, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, seeking treatment and cure by it, let him turn to it with intention, sincerity, and certainty, for it will benefit him, if Allah wills. But if doubt over it has crossed his heart, he should not treat himself with its like; and if he inclines to the word of the physicians where they have spoken against it, then he will gain no benefit from it. It is Allah who grants the success of affirming His friends and submitting to their command, and of receiving and accepting from them, to those of His servants whom He is pleased with and chooses for their guardianship.

**On Seeking Healing Through Acts of Righteousness**

We have narrated from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "In the black seed (al-habba al-sawda) is a cure for every disease except al-sam," that is, death. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali said this to some of his companions, telling them this hadith, and it pleased them, and they said: "O son of the Messenger of Allah, how easy a remedy is this, that heals every disease but death!" He said: "Yes. Shall I not tell you of something easier still, in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ excluded neither death nor anything else?" They said: "What is it, O son of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "Supplication, for it turns back the decree even after it has been firmly sealed." And he joined his fingers together, all of them, bringing the two little fingers side by side, depicting the firm sealing of the decree.

It is narrated of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he missed a man of the Ansar, who came to him after a time, and he said: "What has kept you from us?" He said: "Sickness and poverty, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Shall I not teach you words to call upon Allah with, by which Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will lift that from you?" He said: "Yes, by my father and my mother, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: "Say: There is no power and no strength except through Allah; I place my trust in the Living who does not die. Praise be to Allah, who has taken no son, who has no partner in His dominion, and who has no protector from humiliation; and magnify Him greatly."

From Ali it is narrated that he said: "I complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of a forgetfulness that had come over me, on account of which much of the Quran slipped away from me. He said to me: O Ali, I will teach you words that will drive that from you and fix the Quran firmly in your heart. Say: O Allah, have mercy on me through the forsaking of disobedience to You for as long as You keep me alive; have mercy on me by sparing me what does not concern me; grant me good discernment in what pleases You with me; bind my heart to the keeping of Your Book as You taught it to me; and grant that I recite it in the manner that pleases You."

Among the words he taught for the firm holding of revelation was this: by Your Book give light to my sight, release my tongue, open my chest with it, employ my body in it, and grant me strength through it, for none can grant strength in it but You. He said: I prayed with those words, and Allah established the Quran firmly in my chest.

It was narrated from him that he said: If one of you sets before him a vessel containing food or drink and fears that something in it may harm him, let him name Allah over it and take from it, for nothing harms alongside the name of Allah.

It was narrated from Abu Abd-Allah, (ع), that a man among his companions complained to him of a corruption he found in his stomach, saying that he could eat no food without it harming and distressing him. He said to him: Say the name of Allah over every food you eat, and over every variety of it as you eat it, and it will not harm you. The man did so and was cured.

It was narrated from him that a man among his companions was struck with a whiteness between his eyes and complained of it, for the affliction had taken hold of him and grieved him. He said to him: You must make dua while you are in prostration. The man said: O son of the Messenger of Allah teach me the words to pray with. He said: Say: O Allah, O Most Merciful, O Compassionate, O Hearer of prayers, O Giver of good things, grant me the good of the Hereafter and of this world, turn away from me the evil of them both, and remove from me this affliction that is between my eyes, for it has grieved and saddened me. He did so and was healed.

It was narrated from him that he said: Be eager for charity and give it early in the day, for there is no believer who gives a charity sincerely, desiring by it what is with Allah, except that Allah wards off from him the evil of what descends from the sky on that day, and shields him from it. Then he said: And do not think little of the prayers of the poor for the sick among you, for they are answered on your behalf, though they may not be answered for the poor themselves.

Ismail ibn Ali entered Medina while he was ill, and Abu Abd-Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad came to visit him. When he saw his condition, he said to him: Call for a basket, put wheat in it, and set it before you. Then instruct your servants that when a beggar comes, they bring him in to you, and hand him some of that wheat with your own hand, and ask him to pray to Allah for you. He said: Shall I not rather give them dirhams and dinars? Abu Abd-Allah said: Do what I have commanded you. He did so, and was granted health.

It was narrated from Abu Abd-Allah that he said: Three things drive away forgetfulness and bring on remembrance: reciting the Quran, using the siwak, and fasting.

It was narrated from him that a man among his companions complained to him of how heavily he was overtaken by worry and grief. He said: When anything of that befalls you, pass your hand over the place of your prostration, then draw your hand across your face from the left side of your cheek, and across your forehead to the right side of your cheek, then say: In the name of Allah, there is no god but He, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, He is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. O Allah, remove from me worry and grief. Let him do this three times.

It was narrated from him that he said: Whoever says every day, thirty times, In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful; praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds; and blessed be Allah, the best of creators; and there is no power and no strength except through Allah, the Most High, the Most Great, Allah will ward off from him ninety-nine kinds of affliction, the least of which is madness.

Mention of bearing illness with patience for its reward:

We have narrated from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah that the Messenger of Allah and his family, said: The groaning of the sick man, if he is patient and counts it for reward, is recorded for him as good deeds; but if it is in panic, he is called one given to panic, and there is no reward for him. The full treatment of this matter, and of the reward in illness for the one who is patient and counts it for reward, has its place among the chapters on funerals. It is also narrated from them that a woman came to the Messenger of Allah with a son of hers who was afflicted in his mind, and said: O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah for this son of mine that He may heal him. He said: As you wish. If you wish, I will pray to Allah for him and He will heal him; and if you wish, I will leave him, and there will be no reckoning or punishment upon him. She said: Then leave him, O Messenger of Allah, may Allah's prayers and.

Mention of seeking refuge and the ruqyah:

We have narrated from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah that the Messenger of Allah and his family, would seat al-Hasan and al-Husayn upon his thighs and seek refuge for them, saying: I seek refuge for you both in the perfect words of Allah from every devil and every crawling thing, and from every envious eye. And he would say: Thus did my father Ibrahim, (ع) and his family, seek refuge for his two sons Ismail and Ishaq, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ).

It was narrated from him that Labid ibn al-Asam the Jew, and the Jewish woman Umm Abd-Allah, worked sorcery against him in a cord of red and yellow threads in which they had tied eleven knots, then placed it inside the sheath of a date-palm and lowered it into one of the steps of a well in Medina. So the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, remained unable to hear, to see, to stand, to speak, to eat, or to drink. Then Jibril, (ع), descended with the two chapters of refuge and said to him: Labid ibn al-Asam and the Jewish woman Umm Abd-Allah have worked sorcery against you. He told him where the sorcery lay, and recited over him: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of the Falaq, and Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, to the end of the two chapters. As the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, recited, one knot was loosened and he sat up; he recited again and another knot was loosened, until he had recited eleven times and eleven knots were loosened, and the Prophet, (ع) and his family, sat up free of it. He ordered Ali, who brought him the sorcery from the well in which it had been placed, and he summoned Labid and Umm Abd-Allah and said: What moved you to do what you have done? Then he said to Labid: May Allah not bring you out of this world safe and sound. Labid was a man of wealth and great means. A boy passed by him wearing in his ear an earring worth a dinar, so he snatched it and tore the boy's ear and took it; and for this his hand was cut off and cauterized, yet the bleeding would not stop, and he bled until he died.

Ali said: I fell gravely ill, so that I could find no rest upon my bed, and the Prophet and his family, came to visit me. He said to me: O Ali, the most sorely tried of people in this world are the prophets, then those who come after them, then those who come after them. Rejoice, for this is your share of the chastisement of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, together with the reward laid up for you. Then he said to me: Would you like Allah to lift from you what afflicts you? I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: Say: O Allah, have mercy upon my thin skin and my fragile bone, and I seek refuge in You from the surge of the burning. O Umm Maldam, if you have believed in Allah, then do not eat flesh, do not drink blood, and do not boil over upon the mouth; depart instead to one who claims that there is another god alongside Allah. And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger. Ali said: I said it, and I was healed at that very hour. Jafar ibn Muhammad said: I never turned to it in distress but that I found it answered; and they used to teach it even to women and children.

It was narrated from Ali that the Messenger of Allah and his family, gave license for ruqyah by the Book of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and by what is known of His remembrance and His names. He said: These incantations are among what Sulayman ibn Dawud, (ع), took as authority over the jinn.

It was narrated from him that the Messenger of Allah and his family, said: There is no ruqyah except in three things: a festering wound, an evil eye, or blood. People hold that the ruqyah is for the sting of the scorpion and the sting of the wasp, but that is a mistake. The hummah is the venom in such things, from the scorpion and the serpent and others; the hummah is a venomous creature, while the scorpion's sting is a needle.

It was narrated of the Messenger of Allah and his family, that he sent out a company, and they passed by an Arab tribe whose chief had been stung. They asked whether anyone among them could perform a ruqyah, and one of them recited over him the Opening of the Book, and he was cured. When the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, was told of it, he approved it. One of his wives also performed a ruqyah with the two chapters of refuge, and he approved that, saying to her: And how did you know that it is a ruqyah?

He, may Allah bless him and his family, said: There is no contagion, no ill omen from birds, and no ham; but the evil eye is real and the good omen is real. And he and his family, said: When one of you looks upon a person, or a beast, or anything pleasing that delights him, let him say: I have believed in Allah; may Allah bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad; then his eye will not harm what he looked upon. It was narrated from him that when an eye struck him or a headache came upon him, he would spread out his two hands, recite into them the Opening of the Book and the two chapters of refuge, then wipe his face with them, and what he had been feeling would depart.

He and his family, forbade sorcery, soothsaying, amulets, and tiwalah. Amulets are what is hung upon a person bearing other than the names of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and tiwalah is what women make to draw the love of their husbands to them. Jafar ibn Muhammad said: There is no harm in a charm that is hung if it contains something of the Quran.

A man complained to Abu Abd-Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad of a pain he found in himself. He said: Say In the name of Allah, and wipe over the place, then say: I seek refuge in the might of Allah, I seek refuge in the power of Allah, I seek refuge in the majesty of Allah, I seek refuge in the greatness of Allah, I seek refuge in all the bounds of Allah, I seek refuge in the names of Allah, and I seek refuge in the names of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family, from the evil of what I find. Let him say this seven times. The man said: I said it, and what I had been suffering left me.

It was narrated from him and his family, that he said: When you wish to seek refuge, clasp your two palms together, recite into them the Opening of the Book and Say, He is Allah, One three times, then lay them upon the place of pain; then clasp them again, recite into them the Opening of the Book and Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of the Falaq three times, and lay them upon the pain a second time; then clasp them again, recite into them the Opening of the Book and Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind three times, and lay them upon the pain. Three times in all.

It was narrated from Ali that he said: Whoever is ill-tempered, let the call to prayer be given in his ear. And Abu Abd-Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad said of the sick man who has a ruqyah performed for him: There is no harm in it, so long as the ruqyah is by something known. It was narrated from Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali that he said: When you wish to perform a ruqyah upon a wound, against pain, or blood, or what is feared for it, place your hand upon the wound and say: In the name of Allah I perform your ruqyah; in the name of Allah the Greatest, against iron and stone, and the dark fang and the running of sweat, so let it not deceive, and against the eye, so let it not keep vigil. Repeat it three times.

Mention of treatment and medicine:

We have narrated from the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt that the Messenger of Allah and his family, was asked whether the sick should be treated and given remedies. He said: Yes. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has sent down no disease without sending down a remedy with it, so seek treatment, except for the sam, which is death, for it has no cure.

A group of the Ansar asked him about a man among them who complained of his stomach, and about a Jewish physician who treated such a thing by opening the abdomen. The Messenger of Allah and his family, was reluctant and did not permit them. They returned to him about it two or three times, and each time he refused them, until at last he said to them: Do as you wish. So the Jew was called for, and he opened the man's abdomen, removed a great deal of foul matter from it, then washed the abdomen, stitched it, and treated it, and the man became well. When the Messenger of Allah and his family, was told of it, he said: He who created the disease has appointed for it a remedy; and the best of remedies are cupping, phlebotomy, and the black seed, which is the shuneez. And the Messenger of Allah and his family, forbade imposing strict diets upon the sick.

He looked at Salman, who was eating dates while suffering from sore eyes, and said: O Salman, you eat dates while you have sore eyes? Salman said: O Messenger of Allah, it is only my right eye that is sore, and I am chewing with my left teeth. So the Messenger of Allah smiled and did not stop him.

It was narrated from him and his family, that he said: To forgo the evening meal is a cause of weakness in old age. And he said and his family: Do not force your sick to eat, for Allah the Mighty and Majestic feeds them and gives them drink. It was narrated from him and his family, that there is no harm in an enema, were it not that it enlarges the belly. And he said and his family: When blood becomes excessive in one of you, let him draw it off, even with a small blade, meaning when the blood overcomes him. And he said and his family: Cupping of the head is a cure for every disease, and remedy lies in four things: cupping, the enema, the depilatory, and vomiting.

Ali said: The Messenger of Allah was never seized by fever but that he turned to cupping. And he used to say: When blood becomes excessive in one of you, let him be cupped on whatever day it may be, and let him recite Ayat al-Kursi, seek the forgiveness of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and send blessings upon the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family. Do not hold certain days to be against you, lest they be set against you; be cupped on whichever of them you wish; and let him name Allah over the cupping vessel.

Among the things narrated concerning the body and its remedies is the matter of cupping: the cupping of the head brings relief, and the cupping of the upper back, the kahil, is beneficial. As for fever, it is from the heat of Hell, so it is to be cooled with water; and when the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) was taken with fever, he would call for water and place his hand in it.

Al-Hasan and al-Husayn once fell ill with fever, and Fatima came to the Messenger of Allah seeking help and refuge. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah for your son that He heal him, for he is gravely ill." So the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) rose and came to him, sat at his head, and found him in a heavy state. He said, "O Fatima, it is Allah the Almighty who bestowed him upon you, and He is able to heal him." Then Jibril came to him and said, "O Muhammad, Allah the Almighty has not sent down upon you a sura of the Quran in which there is not a fa, and every fa is an affliction, an afa, save al-Hamd, for there is no fa in it. So call for a cup of water, recite al-Hamd over it forty times, then pour it over him, and Allah the Almighty will heal him." The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) did so, and it was as though the boy had been loosed from a tether.

It is narrated from him that he was asked about cauterisation, and he forbade it. Jafar ibn Muhammad said, "There is no objection to cauterisation. As for what was forbidden, that concerns what is feared to cause death or what disfigures the creation. As for what one hopes will bring a cure, there is nothing wrong with it."

The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) used to command applying kohl with ithmid before sleep, and he would say, "Apply kohl an odd number of times." And he said, "You must use ithmid, for it makes the lashes grow, removes the motes from the eye, and clears the sight." He said ((ع) and his family), "Al-Ajwa is from Paradise, and in it is a cure for poison." Some of the Ahl al-Bayt described its preparation thus: one takes Ajwa dates, removes their stones, pounds them thoroughly, and kneads them with aged cow's ghee; then it is set aside, and when it is needed by one who has taken poison, it is eaten and benefits him.

It is narrated from him that a scorpion stung the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family). He struck it down and said, "May Allah curse you, for you spare neither believer nor disbeliever from your sting." Then he called for salt, placed it upon the place of the sting, and pressed it with his thumb until it dissolved, and said, "If people knew what is in salt, they would have no need of any antidote alongside it."

It is narrated from him that he said, "Whoever eats twenty-one seedless raisins each morning on an empty stomach will not fall ill except with the illness in which he dies." And, "Whoever eats seven dates at his bedtime will be spared colic, and the worms in his belly will be killed." He said to Jafar ibn Abi Talib, "Eat quince, for it strengthens the heart and emboldens the coward."

He said, "Honey is a healing." Jafar ibn Muhammad said that Allah the Almighty has mentioned it in His Book, where He said of it, "فِيهِ شِفَآءٌۭ لِّلنَّاسِ," that is, "In it is a healing for people." He said ((ع) and his family), "Beware of al-shabram, for it is hot; and you must take senna, so treat yourselves with it, for if anything could repel death, senna would repel it. And treat yourselves with fenugreek, for if my nation knew what it holds for them, they would treat themselves with it even were it to cost its weight in gold." He forbade ((ع) and his family) the eating of clay and charcoal, and said that Allah the Almighty created Adam from clay and therefore forbade the eating of clay to his descendants. "Whoever eats clay has aided in his own harm, and whoever persists in eating clay until he dies of it, I will not pray over him." Jafar ibn Muhammad said that the eating of clay breeds hypocrisy.

The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) said that eating fresh, soft fish dissolves the body, so one should not become accustomed to it; and when he ate it he would say, "O Allah, bless it for us and give us in its place what is better than it." Jafar ibn Muhammad said, "Whoever eats fish, let him eat dates afterward, for that removes its harm." The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) forbade the drinking of al-hamim. Al-hamim is the rain that falls in the severity of heat, and al-hamim is also hot water; likewise the rainwater that falls in intense heat and runs along the ground until it grows hot and harmful. For this reason he forbade its drinking, not because it is unlawful or impure, but because it was disliked for the harm it causes.

It is narrated from him that he said, "Whoever is a physician, or one who undertakes treatment, whether Arab or non-Arab, let him not treat anyone until he has obtained a written release from him, witnessed by witnesses. Let him fear Allah the Almighty, strive diligently, and counsel sincerely." By the release he meant that the physician should be learned in medicine and should not treat people while ignorant; for if he does, he is liable for what he destroys.

It is narrated from him that he used to say, "Whoever desires to endure, though there is no enduring, let him lighten his burden, keep to his sandals, take his morning meal early, draw near his evening meal, and lessen intercourse." It was said to him, "O Commander of the Faithful, what is the lightening of the burden?" He replied, "It is debt."

He said, "The truffle is from the manna, and its water is a cure for the eye." Some of the Ahl al-Bayt described its preparation: one takes a truffle and washes it until it is clean, then squeezes its water into a vessel and kindles a fire beneath it until it thickens; then musk is added to it, and it is applied as kohl for all the ailments of the eye. When its moisture dries, it is moistened with rainwater from the sky and applied as kohl. And it is narrated from Ali that he said, "Nothing restores the woman in childbirth like the eating of fresh, moist dates. Allah the Almighty fed Maryam fresh dates in her childbirth." He said, "Eat the pomegranate with its pith, for it is a tanner for the stomach. And you must eat apples, for they cleanse the stomach."

It is narrated from him ((ع) and his family) that the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) said, "Celery is the herb of the prophets, and there is no leaf of endive but that upon it is water from Paradise. You must take the gourd, for it strengthens the heart and the mind." He ((ع) and his family) once trod upon the scorching ground and it burned him, so he stepped onto the purslane, which is the foolish herb, and the heat of the scorching ground subsided for him; so he blessed it, and he used to eat it and was fond of it. Ali said, "The sick are healed by nothing like the drinking of honey."

Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked about a man who seeks treatment from a Jew or a Christian. He said, "There is nothing wrong with that, for healing is in the hand of Allah the Almighty." He was also asked: if a woman has a disease in her body, or a fracture or a wound in a place that is not proper to look upon, may she uncover it to a man who treats her? He said, "There is nothing wrong with that when she is compelled to it." And Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked about a man who treats people with medicine and takes a fee for it, and he said, "There is nothing wrong with it."

It is narrated from him that he said, "If people were moderate in their food and drink, their bodies would remain sound." He said, "Abandoning the evening meal is the ruin of the body." He said, "Allah the Almighty says, وَلَهُمْ رِزْقُهُمْ فِيهَا بُكْرَةًۭ وَعَشِيًّۭا, that is, and they shall have their provision therein, morning and evening." A man complained to him of pains and indigestion that he was suffering, and he said, "Take your midday meal and your evening meal, and eat nothing between them, for that is the corruption of the body." He said, "Abandoning the evening meal diminishes a strength that does not return," and, "Let not the aged man abandon the evening meal, even if it be only a morsel." He said, "Eating meat with milk makes the flesh grow and strengthens the bone." And he said, "A prophet among the prophets complained to Allah the Almighty of his few children, so He commanded him to eat meat with eggs."

It is narrated from him ((ع) and his family) that the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) counseled Ali, saying, "O Ali, sleep upon your back, for it slims your belly; and drink water by sipping, for thereby your food is made wholesome. Wear a ring, and apply kohl an odd number of times, for it will brighten your sight. Anoint yourself every other day, in keeping with the Sunnah of your Prophet. Renew your sandals, for they are the anklets of a man, and turbans are the crowns of the Arabs. When you cook a pot, make its broth plentiful, for if your neighbors do not receive some of its meat, they will receive some of its broth. Wear a ring of ruby and carnelian, for it is fortunate and blessed; whenever a man looks at his face within it, it increases him in light, and the prayer offered wearing it is worth seventy prayers. Wear the ring upon your right hand, for that is the practice of the Messengers, and whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me. Do not wear a ring upon the left, nor of anything but ruby and carnelian."

It is narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad that a man among his companions complained to him of pain in his loin. He said to him, "Take what falls from the table among the food, follow after it, and eat it." The man said, "I did so, and I was healed." Jafar ibn Muhammad said, "Eat of the food that falls from the table, for in it is a healing, by the leave of Allah the Almighty, for whoever seeks healing by it, that is, for every disease." A man looked at apples in the hands of Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad, and he said to him, "The apple cools the heat and quenches it, and removes the fever." He mentioned vinegar and said, "It firms the mouth and kills the worms of the belly." He said, "Rice sawiq, when it is parched and ground, binds the belly; if part of it is made into sawiq and part into a gruel, it binds the belly. Sawiq makes the flesh grow and strengthens the bone, and it benefits the feverish one when it is moistened and washed three times. Take sawiq dry on an empty stomach, for it dispels phlegm and bile." And it is narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn that he permitted treatment with the milk of she-asses, and that if one finds the milk of the wild ass, that is better.

The Body's Portion: Food, Drink, and Healing

edits.body_md:
Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), said: "Dress and adorn yourselves with what is lawful, for Allah, mighty and exalted, loves beauty." It is narrated that he went out one cold day wearing a fur cloak of yellow khazz and a yellow khazz mantle. When he saw the people staring at him, he said: "There was a prophet, the son of a prophet, the son of a prophet, the son of a prophet," meaning Yusuf, (ع), "who wore robes of brocade fastened with gold and sat upon his throne to judge among the people."

Ali ibn al-Husayn, (ع), used to wear in summer two garments bought for five hundred dirhams each, and in winter he wore khazz. Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked about a man who acquires many garments to adorn himself, keeping some in reserve to protect the others, whether this is a kind of excess. He said: "No, that is not extravagance. Allah, mighty and exalted, says: ﴿لِيُنفِقْ ذُو سَعَةٍ مِّن سَعَتِهِ﴾ Let the one who has abundance spend out of his abundance." (Al-Talaq: 7)

> قُلْ مَنْ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَخْرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِۦ وَٱلطَّيِّبَتِ مِنَ ٱلرِّزْقِ

Sufyan al-Thawri came in upon him and saw that he was wearing fine garments. He said: "O son of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, you tell us that Ali, (ع), used to wear coarse cloth and rough fabric, yet here you are dressed in al-Quhi and al-Muwri." He answered: "Woe to you, Sufyan. Ali lived in a time of hardship and scarcity, but Allah, mighty and exalted, has widened our means, and it is fitting for the one upon whom Allah has bestowed abundance that the trace of that bounty be seen upon him." Ali ibn al-Husayn used to have a khazz mantle bought for him for fifty dinars, which he would wear through the winter, entering the mosque and praying in it. When summer came he would order that it be given away as charity on his behalf, and he would command that two garments of the Egyptian sort be bought for him, which would be readied and which he would wear in the summer, wearing between these the fine and the plain alike. When this was remarked upon to him, he would recite the words of Allah, mighty and exalted: ﴿قُلْ مَنْ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي أَخْرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِ وَالطَّيِّبَاتِ مِنَ الرِّزْقِ﴾ "Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants, and the good things of sustenance?" (Al-Araf: 32)

Ali once looked upon a people wearing wool and hair, and he said to them: "Wear cotton, for that was the clothing of the Messenger of Allah, the best thing he could find, and it is our dress. He wore neither wool nor hair, so do not wear them except out of some need, or when you can find nothing else. Allah, mighty and exalted, is beautiful and loves beauty, and He loves to see the trace of His blessing upon His servant."

It is narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad that he performed the Hajj, entering ihram in two fine garments. While he was making tawaf in them, a man tugged at the edge of his cloak. He turned and found it was Abbad al-Basri, who said to him: "O Abu Abdullah, you wear garments such as these, in a place such as this, when you stand in relation to Ali where you stand, and you know what his clothing was like?" He replied, (ع): "Woe to you, Abbad. Ali lived in a time when what he wore was suited to it. If I were to wear his dress today, people would say: This man is a pretender like Abbad al-Basri." Now Abbad was known for ostentation, so he was silenced and shamed, and those around him exchanged glances at his expense.

It is also narrated from him that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: "Wear fine turbans, for they are the crowns of the Arabs." And it is narrated from Abu Jafar Muhammad, (ع), that some of his companions came in upon him while he was in a richly appointed room, furnished with cushions, embroidered coverings, armrests, and bedding. Later they came in upon him again and found him in a room furnished with a reed mat. They said to him: "May we be your ransom, what is this room?" He said: "This is my room. The room you saw before is the woman's room. Let me tell you something my father told me. He said: Some people once came in upon al-Husayn and in his dwelling were carpets, rugs, and many furnishings. They said: O son of the Messenger of Allah, we see in your house things that were not in the house of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family. He said: We marry women and give them their dowries, with which they furnish and prepare their homes."

As for clothing, then, whether fine or plain, to wear it, to spread it out, and to wrap oneself in it are all permissible, and there is nothing disliked in this. Whoever wears the plain out of humility while he could have otherwise, there is nothing against him; and whoever wears the fine, finding it within his reach and his means, that too is permissible for him, and indeed it is recommended as a showing of the grace of Allah, mighty and exalted. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, wore both the fine and the plain, whatever he wore and whatever others clothed him in.

On What Is Lawful, Forbidden, and Disliked in Clothing

It is narrated to us from the Imams, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), that clothing made of whatever the earth grows, and the spreading of it, the wrapping in it, and the praying in it and upon it, are all lawful. Likewise the skin of every animal whose flesh may be eaten, and its wool, hair, and fur, are lawful and permitted, so long as the animal was slaughtered properly. As for the wool, hair, and fur of a dead animal, and its skin, to wrap oneself in it, spread it out, and use it is permitted, as we have mentioned, just as the like is permitted in what has been touched by impurities, except that one may not pray in any of it, just as one does not pray in an impure garment.

> وَأَعِدُّوا۟ لَهُم مَّا ٱسْتَطَعْتُم مِّن قُوَّةٍۢ وَمِن رِّبَاطِ ٱلْخَيْلِ تُرْهِبُونَ بِهِۦ عَدُوَّ

The Imams disliked for a man to wear pure silk, though they permitted what was woven together with something else grown from the earth. It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, permitted it to certain people, and allowed that one display it and adorn oneself with it before the enemy, so that they might know the strength of the Muslims, in keeping with the words of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿وَأَعِدُّوا لَهُم مَّا اسْتَطَعْتُم مِّن قُوَّةٍ وَمِن رِّبَاطِ الْخَيْلِ تُرْهِبُونَ بِهِ عَدُوَّ اللَّهِ﴾ "And prepare against them whatever force you are able, and steeds of war, by which you strike fear into the enemy of Allah." (Al-Anfal: 60) The Imams would themselves wear it in this manner, woven with other materials, and lined with what the earth grows, displaying it before the enemies of Allah, and they permitted it to whoever would so display it. Even though the world and all that is in it is among the most trifling of things in their sight, they would show of it only what they showed as a preparation for the strength of Islam and the Muslims, and a display before those who set themselves against them and made enmity with them among all people.

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, used to love white among garments and would say: "It is the best of your clothing, so wear it, and shroud your dead in it." No dye renders a garment forbidden to wear. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, and the Imams of his house wore dyed cloth, while preferring some dyes over others. As is narrated from Ali that he said: "Saffron is ours, and safflower yellow is for the Banu Umayyah." And Jafar ibn Muhammad disliked a deep, heavily saturated red, saying: "It is the garb of Qarun and the dye of the Banu Umayyah." He used to wear safflower that was not intense. It is narrated of Ali that he went out to the people of Kufa one day, from the palace to the open ground of al-Rahba, wearing a yellow waist-wrapper and a black khamisa, with sandals on his feet and in his hand an anaza, that is, a staff upon which he leaned.

It is narrated of Jafar ibn Muhammad that he entered ihram in a green cloak, and of Ali ibn al-Husayn that he was seen wearing a black overgarment with a blue border. Yet the Imams, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), disliked black as adornment, because the Banu al-Abbas had taken it as their garb and claimed that they wore it in grief for al-Husayn ibn Ali. Had there been any merit in this, it would have been the duty of the Imams among his own descendants to be the first to it; and had they truly grieved for him as they claimed, they would not have done to his descendants what they did. So the Imams, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), disliked adorning themselves in the garb of such people. They saw no harm in images or figures worked into garments. It is narrated from one of the companions of Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali that he came in upon him while he was seated on a carpet bearing figures, and spoke to him about it. He said that the sunnah is that one tread upon it. And when the dislike that some people hold for living figures was mentioned before him, on the grounds that Allah, mighty and exalted, created such things, he said: "Is it not He, mighty and exalted, who created everything, the trees and the inanimate, all that is seen? Yet they portray that and see no harm in portraying it. So what is the difference between the one and the other?"

On Ornaments and What May Be Made of Them

It is narrated to us from the Imams of the house of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, all of them, that they related from him that he permitted women to adorn themselves with gold. Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked about this, and he said: "My father used to adorn his children and his women with gold and silver." He said: "There is no harm in ornamenting swords and copies of the Quran with gold and silver." It is narrated of Ali that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, say: "A woman should not pray except with an earring upon her or more," meaning when she is able to find such a thing. He forbade women to leave themselves bare of ornament, and to imitate men, and he cursed those among them who did so. Jafar ibn Muhammad said: "It is not fitting for a woman to leave herself unadorned, even if only by hanging a necklace about her neck." And the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, forbade women, when they go out, to wear ornaments that make an audible sound, in keeping with the words of Allah, mighty and exalted: ﴿وَلَا يَضْرِبْنَ بِأَرْجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعْلَمَ مَا يُخْفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّ﴾ "And let them not strike their feet so as to make known what they conceal of their adornment." (Al-Nur: 31)

It is narrated from him that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, forbade men to set a seal-ring of gold. His own seal, may Allah bless him and his family, was of silver, its stone of silver as well, engraved with "Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah." The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, forbade the setting of rings of iron and adorning oneself with iron, saying: "It is the ornament of the people of the Fire." It is narrated from him that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, used to wear his ring on his right hand, and likewise it has come from the Imams that they wore their rings on their right hands and commanded their followers and adherents to do the same.

It is narrated of Ali that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, say: "Whoever sets a ring with a stone of red carnelian, Allah seals his affair with what is good." He used to recommend it, and the ruby as well, and would say: "Each time a man looks into it, light increases upon his face, and the prayer wearing it is worth seventy prayers." And he said: "How excellent a stone is crystal." The engraving of the seal of Ali was "Ali believes in Allah." Jafar ibn Muhammad forbade the setting of a ring whose stone bears an engraved figure, and the engraving of his own seal was "My Lord, You are my trust, so protect me from the evil of Your creation." It is narrated of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, that he used to turn his ring so that its stone lay against the inside of his palm.

On Fragrance, Its Excellence, and Its Recommendation

It is narrated to us from the Imams of the house of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, from Ali that he said: "Three things were given to the prophets: fragrance, marriage, and the siwak." And the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family, when he traveled, carried certain things with him: the flask, the shears, the kohl-vessel, the mirror, the comb, and the siwak. He said, may Allah bless him and his family: "No servant's garment is cleansed but that his faults are lessened, and his scent is not made sweet but that his understanding is increased."

Jafar ibn Muhammad said: "A sweet fragrance strengthens the heart and increases vigor. The fragrance of men is that whose scent is apparent and whose color is hidden, and the fragrance of women is that whose color is apparent and whose scent is concealed, except when they go out, for then it is disliked that they perfume themselves so that it can be detected from them." It is narrated of Ali that he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, used to apply fragrance, and to apply it abundantly, until it would change the color of his hair. And he said, may Allah bless him and his family: "Whoever goes to the Friday prayer, let him apply perfume, even if only from his family's flask." It is narrated of Ali that he would sometimes perfume himself from the fragrance of his wives, by which is meant the kind of women's fragrance whose color does not show but only its scent. As for what shows its color, such as khaluq and the like, it is disliked for men except in the company of their wives. The Imams disliked that one return a gift of fragrance to him who offered it, and likewise that one refuse an offering of water.

Al-Muizz, (ع), said: Al-Mansur, may Allah sanctify his soul, told me: One day, when I was a small boy, I was present at the table of al-Mahdi, (ع), and we were a company of his sons and his sons sons eating before him, with a serving-girl standing by with water for us. She offered it to one of the boys, who refused it, and al-Mahdi rebuked her sharply and said: "Were it not for the sanctity of your sharing in this food, I would have disciplined you well. What moved you to offer him water when he had not asked for it?" Then he said to the boy: "And you, when it was offered to you, why did you refuse it? Water is too noble a thing to be offered to one who did not ask, or to be refused by one to whom it was offered." Al-Mansur, (ع), said: I did not understand at the time what manner of thing this was, but when I came to understand, I grasped his meaning. And so it is with fragrance as well.

From Ali it is narrated that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, used to anoint himself with musk, المسك. He held it in such regard that he directed it be placed in his embalming, his حنوط, so that its fragrance would remain with him. And something finer than it was used over him in that embalming.

It is further narrated, on the authority of the Imams that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, forbade a woman to pray unless she has applied henna, الحناء, or has touched the place of the henna with something.

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali said that a woman should therefore not leave off the dye, الخضاب, even when she has grown old, even if she does no more than wipe her hand with henna as a light anointing. And she should not make herself resemble men.

And from Ali it is narrated that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: "It is not for a menstruating woman to tell a story or to engrave."

And from Ali: "The Children of Israel perished through stories, engravings, henna, and excessive ornamentation."

edits.body_md:
### What is lawful in hunting and what is forbidden

> أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ صَيْدُ ٱلْبَحْرِ وَطَعَامُهُۥ مَتَعًۭا لَّكُمْ وَلِلسَّيَّارَةِ ۖ وَحُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ صَيْدُ ٱلْبَرِّ مَا دُمْتُمْ حُرُمًۭا

Allah the Almighty said: ﴿أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ صَيْدُ الْبَحْرِ وَطَعَامُهُ مَتَاعًا لَكُمْ وَلِلسَّيَّارَةِ وَحُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ صَيْدُ الْبَرِّ مَا دُمْتُمْ حُرُمًا﴾ "He has made permissible for you the hunting of the sea and its food, as a pleasure for you and for travelers, and forbidden for you is the hunting of land as long as you are in the sacred state" (al-Maidah: 96), and He said: ﴿وَإِذَا حَلَلْتُمْ فَاصْطَادُوا﴾ "But when you leave the sacred state, then hunt" (al-Maidah: 2). So the Almighty permitted the hunting of the sea even while one remains in the state of consecration, and forbade the hunting of the land while one is in it. He addressed this to the generality of the believers, except for what was excluded from it on the tongue of His Messenger and the Imams of his household, who make plain what He intends, as He says: ﴿وَأَنزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الذِّكْرَ لِتُبَيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ مَا نُزِّلَ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ "And We have sent down to you the Remembrance that you may make clear to the people what has been revealed to them" (al-Nahl: 44).

We have narrated from the Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, that he forbade hunting birds in their nests, and said: "The bird in its nest is under the protection of Allah; but if it takes to the air upon its wings, then hunt it if you wish. Set a trap for it and shoot at it." It was narrated from him, and from Ali, (ع), and from Jafar ibn Muhammad, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), that pigeons in the towns should not be hunted, because they are among what belongs to their owners, even when they fly free. We have already mentioned, in the chapters on food, what is lawful to eat among the beasts of land and sea and what is forbidden. So whatever is caught of that which is lawful to eat is eaten, and whatever is caught of that which is forbidden to eat is left and not eaten, except in dire necessity for the one who is compelled.

### What hunting animals seize and kill

> عَلَيْهِ ۖ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ

Allah the Almighty said: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ قُلْ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ الطَّيِّبَاتُ وَمَا عَلَّمْتُم مِّنَ الْجَوَارِحِ مُكَلِّبِينَ تُعَلِّمُونَهُنَّ مِمَّا عَلَّمَكُمُ اللَّهُ فَكُلُوا مِمَّا أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَاذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ﴾ "They ask you what has been made lawful for them. Say: Lawful for you are all good things, and what you have trained of hunting animals, training them as Allah has taught you, so eat of what they have caught for you, and mention the name of Allah over it, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning" (al-Maidah: 4).

We have narrated from the Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, from Ali and upon them all, that he said: If a hunting animal seizes prey and it dies before its slaughter can be performed, then if the animal is trained, and the Muslim sent it and invoked the name of Allah at its release, it may be eaten. If he forgot to invoke the name at the moment of release, he invokes it when he remembers. But if he deliberately omitted it, it is not to be eaten.

The word الجوارح in the tongue of the Arabs, the tongue in which the Quran was revealed, means the earners. The Arabs say, "So-and-so is the جارحة of his household," meaning the one who earns for them. So dogs and their like, and the birds of prey with which one hunts, are earners that earn the catch for the one who has trained them. If such an animal is untrained yet seizes the prey, and the prey is reached while still alive and is then slaughtered, it is eaten; but if its slaughter is not reached in time, it is not eaten. And they, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), said: Whatever the trained hunting animals seize may be eaten, even if its slaughter was not reached, and even if the animal has eaten from it. They said: Every trained hunting creature, such as cheetahs and the other predators of the land, and the birds of prey, may have its catch eaten.

They narrated from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, concerning the hunting of the black dog, that he disliked it for them and ordered it to be killed. And they said: Dogs are all one in their ruling, apart from this, whether the Kurdish kind or the greyhound kind: what they seize may be eaten when they are trained. They said: If the prey is reached while still alive and the hunting animal has wounded it, and he does not then slaughter it, and it dies in his hands from the act of the hunting animal, it is eaten. But if the hunting animal did not wound it, and it was carried off and died afterward, he does not eat it.

From Ali that he forbade the eating of whatever dies before its slaughter can be reached from the game of the dogs of the Magians and of the Christians of the Arabs, and of whatever hunting animals they have trained, unless the Muslims train them afterward.

### What hunters bring down with a throw

> ٱعْتَدَىٰ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَلَهُۥ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌۭ

Allah the Almighty said: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَيَبْلُوَنَّكُمُ اللَّهُ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنَ الصَّيْدِ تَنَالُهُ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَرِمَاحُكُمْ لِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ مَن يَخَافُهُ بِالْغَيْبِ فَمَنِ اعْتَدَى بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَلَهُ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ "O you who believe, Allah will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and your spears can reach, that Allah may know who fears Him in the unseen. So whoever transgresses after that, for him is a painful punishment" (al-Maidah: 94).

We have narrated from the Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah, (ع), that one of them said to a man who asked him about hunting, when he throws at prey, strikes it, and it dies: "Eat what you have killed outright (al-isma), and do not eat what you have driven off (al-inma)." Al-isma is that a man throws at the quarry and strikes it, and it dies on the spot. Al-inma is that he strikes it and it moves off and goes out of his sight until it is hidden from him and disappears, and then it dies and he finds it dead, and he does not know whether it died from his blow or from something else.

It has been narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad that he said: If he shoots the game with an arrow and strikes it in a fatal spot, then it disappears from him, and he later finds his arrow in it and knows that it died from his shot, he may eat it. But if he does not know that, he does not eat it. From Ali that he said: If he shoots the game and strikes it, and then it falls from a high place or falls into water and dies, he does not eat it, unless he knows that it died from the blow that struck it.

Everything we have mentioned of what game is shot or struck with, so that it dies, is lawful to eat only when it has been struck with a sword, a spear, an arrow, or an iron implement. As for whatever is struck of that with a stick, a stone, or a pellet, it is not eaten according to the word of the people of the household unless its slaughter is reached while it is alive. They permitted the مِعْراض when one has no other arrow: the مِعْراض is an arrow without feathers, which is thrown and strikes the game with its body. From Ali that he said: Whatever the snare takes of game, and it dies in it before it is slaughtered, is not eaten. But if it severs a hand, a leg, or a limb and cuts it off, and its slaughter is then reached, it is eaten, except for the severed limb. The الحبالة is what is set up to take game, such as nets, traps, and the like.

### The Comprehensive Doors of Slaughter

### The acts of those who slaughter

We have narrated from the Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, that they narrated from him that he said: "Whoever slaughters an animal, let him sharpen his blade and let him give his animal ease."

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, (ع), said: When you intend to slaughter an animal, do not torment the beast. Sharpen the blade, face the qiblah, and invoke the name of Allah, and do not sever it through until it dies, meaning do not cut off its head. Likewise he forbade that it be skinned until it has died and grown still. They said: Whoever slaughters and forgets the invocation of the name, or to face the animal toward the qiblah, or is unaware of it, invokes the name of Allah the Almighty when he remembers, and it may be eaten. But if he deliberately omits that, his slaughtered animal is not to be eaten. And if he says "There is no god but Allah," or "Allah is the Greatest," or remembers Allah the Almighty with whatever he may remember Him, that suffices him in place of the invocation. What they recommended to say at the slaughter is, "In the name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest."

They narrated from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, that he forbade mutilating beasts and ordered that they be slaughtered as is due, and forbade المجثمة and الْمَصْبُورَةُ, which is the beast that is held, or buried, or tied up, and shot at until it dies. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali said: Whoever kills a sparrow in vain, Allah the Almighty will bring it before him on the Day of Resurrection, and it will cry out, saying, "My Lord, ask this one why he killed me without slaughter." So beware of mutilation.

He said: Slaughter is at the place of slaughter, that is, below the غلصمة. The غلصمة is the knot in the windpipe, and it should be left in the head. The slaughterer cuts the windpipe, the gullet, and the two jugular veins, falling short of none of that, and not cutting into the bone. That is the Sunnah of slaughter. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali and upon his family, was asked about breaking the neck of the animal before it dies, and he disliked it. They said: Whoever the knife outruns, or who out of ignorance cuts off the head of the animal without intending it and without knowing that it is not permitted, there is nothing against him and his animal may be eaten. But if he intends that, he has done wrong, and his animal is not to be eaten.

They said: If the beast bolts, that is, flees or refuses, so that one cannot slaughter it, or it falls into a well and cannot be lifted out, nor can one reach the place of slaughter, then let it be stabbed with a spear, or struck with a sword, or struck with an iron implement until it dies, and it is eaten. They said: There is no slaughter except with iron. Do not slaughter with a stone, nor a tooth, nor a nail, nor a bone, nor anything else, but only with iron.

### What may be eaten of slaughtered animals and what may not

We have narrated from the Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, and upon them all, that he disliked the slaughter of the milk-giving animal and of the pregnant one, though he did not forbid it; rather he disliked it for the benefit in them to one who has nothing else.

> فَكُلُوا۟ مِمَّا ذُكِرَ ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ إِن

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali was asked about the slaughtered animals of the Jews, the Christians, the Magians, and the people of divergent belief, and he recited the word of Allah the Almighty: ﴿فَكُلُوا مِمَّا ذُكِرَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ إِن كُنتُم بِآيَاتِهِ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ "So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs" (al-Anam: 118), and he said: When you hear them invoking the name of Allah, then eat; and what they do not invoke the name of Allah over, do not eat. And whoever among them is suspected of abandoning the invocation, holding it lawful to do so, his slaughtered animal need not be eaten, unless one sees him at the time he slaughters it and hears from him that he has invoked the name of Allah the Almighty over it. Jafar ibn Muhammad said: There is no harm in the meat sold in the markets of the Muslims, as long as it is not known of the slaughterers that they depart from the Sunnah in slaughter, and as long as that is not witnessed of their practice.

From them that they disliked the slaughtered animals of the Magians and the Christians of the Arabs. They permitted the slaughter of the blind man when he is directed toward the qiblah and slaughters well; and likewise the woman when she does it well; and the boy before he reaches maturity when he does it well and there is need of him. They saw no harm in slaughter performed without ritual purity. They permitted the slaughter of the mute when he understands the invocation and gestures with it.

### Valid and invalid slaughter

We have narrated from the Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, from Ali that he was asked about the foetuses of livestock whose mothers are slaughtered while they are in their wombs, whether they are made lawful when they are brought out. He said: "Their slaughter is the slaughter of their mothers, for the foetus is a limb of her limbs. But if it comes out alive, it is left until it dies, and then it is eaten, provided it has grown hair or fur or has something of that upon it, even on its tail, for the tail is the first place where hair appears." And he disliked whatever has not yet grown hair or fur.

He was asked about certain limbs of an animal that are cut while it is alive, such as the fatty tails of sheep, the humps of camels, and the like, and he said: "Whatever is cut from them and separated from them while they are alive, before slaughter, is carrion and is not eaten, and the rest of the animal is not eaten when it is slaughtered." And he said: Valid slaughter is known by the eye that flickers, the leg that kicks, the tail that moves, or the ear. So whoever slaughters his animal and it moves, or thrashes after the slaughter, or flickers its eye, or any part of it stirs, it is validly slaughtered.
