And whatever of it falls and is slaughtered, and nothing of it moves, is not eaten, even if blood came out of it.

He was asked about the animal that is slaughtered and then falls from a height or falls into water and dies, and he said: "If you have done the slaughter well and fulfilled what is required in it, then eat." From Jafar ibn Muhammad that he said: The Sunnah for the large animals is that they be sacrificed standing with one leg bound, and thus did the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, sacrifice his gift-offering. There is no harm, if that is not possible, in its kneeling and being hobbled. He disliked that the sheep be slaughtered standing, except for a reason, and said the Sunnah is that it be laid down; but if it is sacrificed in the manner of the large animals, there is no harm. He was asked about the animal slaughtered from behind the nape, and he said: If one is unaware of that, there is no harm; but if he intends it while knowing the Sunnah, his animal is not eaten and he is to be corrected. He was asked about two sheep, one validly slaughtered and the other not, when the valid one of the two is not known, and he said: Neither of them is eaten until it is known which is validly slaughtered.

### The sacrificial offerings

We have narrated from the Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, and from him that he addressed the people before the Day of Sacrifice and said: "O people, whoever has the means, let him sacrifice and let him magnify the rites of Allah. And whoever does not have the means, then Allah the Almighty does not burden a soul beyond its capacity."

From him that a man of the Ansar met him on the Day of Sacrifice after he had finished the prayer and said, "O Messenger of Allah, if you would honor me with your presence today, for I have prepared food for you." So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, went with him, and the man brought him the food and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I slaughtered my sacrifice before I went out to the place of prayer, and I ordered my family and they prepared this food, that I might be foremost in bringing it to you." The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said to him: "Your sheep is a sheep of meat. If you have another besides it, sacrifice with it." He said, "I have nothing but a young goat of mine." He said: "Sacrifice with it, though it will not be lawful for anyone after you."

So the Sunnah in the sacrifice is that it is not slaughtered except after the Eid prayer on the Day of Sacrifice. Whoever slaughters before the prayer, that does not count for him as a sacrifice, and he must repeat it when he is able. The best slaughter is on the Day of Sacrifice, and it is valid during the days of Mina, which are the Day of Sacrifice, the Day of al-Adha, or the three days after it. Jafar ibn Muhammad said: Among camels and cattle nothing suffices as a sacrifice except the mature animal, and likewise among goats; but the yearling of the sheep suffices. And he said: The sacrifice is an obligation upon every Muslim except one who cannot find the means, and a man's sacrifice suffices for his household.

They narrated from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, that he addressed the people on the Day of Sacrifice and said: "This is the day of العَجّ and الثَّجّ. الثَّجّ is the blood you pour out, and whoever's intention is sincere, its first drop is an expiation for every sin. And العَجّ is supplication, so cry out to Allah the Almighty. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no one will leave this standing-place except that he is forgiven, save the one persisting in a great sin among the great sins, who does not bring himself to forsake it."

From him, may Allah bless him and his family, that he entered upon Fatimah, (ع), on the Day of Sacrifice and said: "O Fatimah, arise and witness your sacrifice, for its first dropping drop is an expiation for every sin that is yours. Its flesh, its dung, its bones, its wool, and everything of it will be placed in your balance and multiplied for you seventy times over." Al-Miqdad heard that and said: "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah, is this something singled out for the family of Muhammad, or is it general?" He said: "Rather it is for the Muslims in general."

Jafar ibn Muhammad said: What is recommended for a man is that he undertake the slaughter of his sacrifice with his own hand. If he is unable, let him place his hand with the hand of the slaughterer. If he is unable to do that, let him stand over it, invoking the name of Allah upon it until it is slaughtered. From Ali that he said: The sacrifice of a Muslim should not be slaughtered except by a Muslim, and he says when slaughtering it: "In the name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. I have turned my face toward the One who created the heavens and the earth, upright and submitting, and I am not among the polytheists. Truly my prayer, my sacrifice, my living, and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds, who has no partner. By this I have been commanded, and I am the first of those who submit."

From Jafar ibn Muhammad that he was asked about the best of sacrificial animals and said: "The females of camels, then their males, then the females of cattle, then their males, then the rams of the sheep, then the wethers of them," meaning those whose testicles have been crushed or bound until they spoil, "then the ewes, then the male of the goats, then the females of them." He disliked the one with cut-off ears. The best of all these kinds is the fattest and the largest of them. The best of the rams is the horned ram that eats amid blackness, drinks amid blackness, walks amid blackness, looks amid blackness, urinates amid blackness, and drops dung amid blackness. With the like of this the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, used to sacrifice. It is the الأملح, the black-and-white. It has come down that he used to sacrifice with two such black-and-white rams, and it is said that this is the description of the ram that was sent down to Ibrahim, (ع) and upon his family.

From Jafar ibn Muhammad that he permitted sharing in the sacrifice for one who cannot find an animal to offer alone but is able to take part. From Ali that he disliked sacrificing the animal with a broken horn, the clearly lame, the clearly emaciated, and the one whose ear has been wholly cut away. He permitted the slit in the ear when it is a mark, and the aged animal when there is no defect or leanness in it. He said: Whoever buys a sacrifice and it falls ill or dies before the Day of Sacrifice, it has sufficed for him; but if he obtains another to sacrifice in its place and does so, that is better.

> فَكُلُوا۟ مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا۟ ٱلْقَانِعَ وَٱلْمُعْتَرَّ

From Jafar ibn Muhammad that he was asked about the word of Allah the Almighty, ﴿فَكُلُوا مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا الْقَانِعَ وَالْمُعْتَرَّ﴾ "So eat of it and feed the contented and the petitioner" (al-Hajj: 36), and His word, ﴿فَكُلُوا مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا الْبَائِسَ الْفَقِيرَ﴾ "So eat of it and feed the wretched poor" (al-Hajj: 28). He said: "The قانع is the beggar who is content with what he is given and does not deem it too little; the مُعْتَرّ is the one who presents himself for charity but does not ask; the poor man is the one who finds nothing, and the مسكين is harder pressed than he in his condition; and the wretched poor man is the worst of them in condition and the most hard pressed."

He said: My father, (رض), when he slaughtered his sacrifice at Mina or sacrificed his gift-offering, would place the head before him. When a beggar passed by, he would stop him and say, "Take the head." If he saw that the man took it with gladness and went on his way, he would give it to him; but he would say, "Leave it," and give him of the meat instead. And if the man turned away from it and did not accept it, he would leave it and give him nothing, testing thereby the conditions of the poor.

> فَكُلُوا۟ مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا۟ ٱلْقَانِعَ وَٱلْمُعْتَرَّ

From Ali that he said concerning the word of Allah the Almighty, ﴿فَكُلُوا مِنْهَا﴾ "So eat of it" (al-Hajj: 36): "This is a command of recommendation, not of obligation. Whoever wishes may eat of his sacrifice, and whoever wishes need not eat of it, and to eat of it is better." It has come down from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, that he made Ali a partner in a gift-offering, and they were a hundred sacrificial camels. He ordered that a piece be taken from each camel and put in a pot and cooked. Then he called Ali and the two of them ate of the meat as much as they could and were able, and sipped of the broth, that they might partake of all their flesh. And the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "The broth is one of the two meats, for the strength of the meat comes out into it." And Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked...

The Hunt and the Knife: Game, Slaughter, and Sacrifice

Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), was asked about a man whom fear of Allah Almighty had so overtaken that he abandoned women, abandoned wholesome food, and grew unable to lift his head toward heaven out of reverence for Allah Almighty. The one who put the question said, "As for his turning away from women, I know what the Messenger of Allah, (ع), had of them. And as for his turning away from wholesome food, the Messenger of Allah used to eat meat and honey. And as for the fear of Allah Almighty entering him until he could no longer raise his head toward the sky out of reverence, who was ever more fearful of Allah, or more humbled before Him, than the Messenger of Allah yet he did not do this?" For Allah Almighty has said, *"Indeed in the Messenger of Allah you have a good example,"* and true humility is in the heart.

> إِن يَكُونُوا۟ فُقَرَآءَ يُغْنِهِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ

This is the spirit in which the merits of marriage are to be understood, for there is no monasticism in Islam. Allah Almighty said: *"And marry the unmarried among you and the righteous among your male and female slaves. If they should be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing."*

It is narrated from the Imams of the House of the Messenger of Allah that he said: "Whoever loves to follow my way among my nation, let him know that marriage is one of my Sunnahs." And he said: "Whoever loves to meet Allah pure and purified, let him meet Him with a wife." And he said: "There is no young man who marries in his youth except that his devil cries out, Woe to him, he has protected two-thirds of his religion! So let the servant then fear Allah Almighty in the remaining third." Whenever he learned that one of his companions had married, he would say, "He has completed his religion." And he said, (ع), "The more a believer increases in faith, the more he loves women." And he said, "There is no monasticism in Islam. Marry, for I shall boast of your numbers before the nations." He forbade celibacy and the forsaking of marriage.

He said: "When a believing man comes to his believing wife, two angels enfold him, and he is like one who has drawn his sword in the path of Allah. When he is done, his sins fall from him as the leaves fall from the tree, as though he had washed himself clean of sin. If she conceives by him, he has the reward of one who fasts and stands in prayer. When the pangs of labor seize her, no one knows her reward but Allah Almighty. When she delivers, with every draft of milk she suckles the child Allah Almighty writes for her a good deed and erases from her an evil one. And if she should die of her travail, she will rise on the Day of Resurrection without reckoning, for she died of her affliction."

And he said: "Whoever abandons marriage out of fear of household expense has thought ill of his Lord the Almighty, who says, *If they should be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty."* And he said: "Whoever amasses wealth and does not marry, so that the women left unwed because of him fall into sin, their sin rests upon him." And from Jafar ibn Muhammad: "No two believers are joined in a lawful marriage but that a caller from heaven cries out, Allah Almighty has wedded such a one to such a one; and no two believing spouses are parted from a marriage but that a caller from heaven cries out, Allah Almighty has permitted the separation of such a one from such a one."

On what is recommended in a spouse, and from whose marriage one should turn away, it is narrated from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah and his family, that he said: "Choose well for your seed, for the maternal uncle is one of the two who share the bed." By this he meant: do not place your seed except in purity, that the mother of the child be not of corrupt origin nor corrupt in herself. From this also he forbade that a child be suckled by the milk of a wicked woman; and if such a thing is disliked in nursing and forbidden, then in lineage it is graver still and more emphatic. He said: "Marry those who are your equals, and give your daughters in marriage to them, and choose well for your seed."

He related that Allah Almighty says: "When I wish to grant My servant the good of this world and the Hereafter, I give him a tongue that remembers Me, a humble heart, a body patient in affliction, and a believing wife who gladdens him when he looks upon her and guards herself and his wealth in his absence." And he said: "Five things are of happiness: a righteous wife, upright children, righteous companions, a man's provision in his own land, and love for the family of Muhammad, (ع) and his family."

He said: "A good woman among women is like the albino crow, and the albino crow is seldom found." By "good" here he meant the believing, chaste, beautiful woman, fitting in all her states; and rare is the woman found in such a condition, so he likened her to the albino crow, which is the rarest of birds. He said: "A woman of standing has no price, neither the good among them nor the bad. As for the good, she has no price in gold or silver or all the possessions of this world; and as for the bad, she has no price, not even of dust, for dust is better than she." And he said: "The world is but enjoyment, and the best enjoyment of the world is a righteous wife." And he said: "Of the believing man's happiness is a righteous wife, a spacious dwelling, an easy mount, and a righteous child."

He forbade that a woman be married for her wealth or her beauty alone, saying, "Her wealth makes her overbearing, and her beauty destroys her." And he said: "Take the one of religion." And he said, comparing what is most prized: "There is no horse finer than the deep black, and no woman like the daughter of one's age." And he said: "The best of your women are the women of Quraysh, the most tender toward a husband and the most devoted to a child."

He said: "Marry the one of clear, healthy complexion, for there is blessing in that. And when one of you would marry a woman, let him ask about her hair as he asks about her face, for the hair is one of the two beauties. And keep to those of shorter stature, for that is better suited to what you seek." He said: "A woman is but a necklace, so let each of you consider well with what he adorns himself." And he said: "If there is ill fortune in anything, it is in a woman, a dwelling, and a mount."

He said: "Women are four: a gathering that gathers, a spring that gives water, a war that subdues, and a galling fetter." As for the galling fetter, the people of the Age of Ignorance would shackle their captives and those they wished to torment with a thong of fresh hide stripped from a camel, turning the hair inward against the skin and binding it fast; as it dried it tightened and the skin contracted, and lice would breed within it and could not be reached because of its tightness, so the captive suffered greatly, a torment that struck without a blow. This the Prophet, (ع), made a likeness of the bad wife and what her husband endures from her. The gathering that gathers is she in whom is gathered her goodness and her purity; the spring that gives water is she who has a child in her arms and another in her womb; and the war that subdues is she of ill manners toward her husband.

> وَلَدٌۭ ۚ فَإِن كَانَ لَكُمْ وَلَدٌۭ فَلَهُنَّ ٱلثُّمُنُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُم ۚ مِّنۢ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍۢ تُوصُونَ بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍۢ ۗ وَإِن كَانَ رَجُلٌۭ يُورَثُ كَلَلَةً أَوِ ٱمْرَأَةٌۭ وَلَهُۥٓ أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌۭ فَلِكُلِّ وَحِدٍۢ مِّنْهُمَا ٱلسُّدُسُ ۚ فَإِن كَانُوٓا۟ أَكْثَرَ مِن ذَلِكَ فَهُمْ شُرَكَآءُ فِى ٱلثُّلُثِ ۚ مِنۢ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍۢ يُوصَىٰ بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍ غَيْرَ مُضَآرٍّۢ ۚ وَصِيَّةًۭ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَلِيمٌۭ

He said: "Beware of marrying the foolish woman, for her companionship is an affliction and her child is a loss." And he said: "The best women of my nation are those fairest of face and lightest in dowry." And he said: "Among the blessings of a woman is that her firstborn be a girl." He said again: "Women are four: a spring that gives water, a gathering that gathers, a war that subdues, and a barren woman." And he said: "Marry the dark-complexioned woman who is fertile, and do not marry the beautiful barren woman, for I will boast of your numbers before the nations on the Day of Resurrection. The children who die young are beneath the Throne of the Most Merciful, seeking forgiveness for their parents; Ibrahim, (ع), takes them into his care, and Sarah raises them upon a mountain of musk and amber and saffron."

He said: "The best of your women is the ardent yet chaste one, ardent toward her husband and chaste from all besides him." And he said: "Marry the virgins, for they are sweetest of mouth, purest of womb, quickest of the women to learn, and most steadfast in affection." And he said: "Marry the ayyami," meaning Allah Almighty will better their character, broaden their provision, and increase their blessing. His command here is to marry the ayyami, those women who once had husbands who died or who divorced them, and it is a command of encouragement, not of obligation that may not be left, just as Allah's word, *"And marry the unmarried among you,"* is of this kind. Whoever marries one of the ayyami, desiring what Allah Almighty and His Messenger have urged, has done what he was called to; and whoever marries a virgin, there is no fault in that, for the virtue of marrying virgins has already been mentioned from the Messenger of Allah. Yet the ayyami should not be passed over out of mere preference or disdain on account of a prior marriage, for most of the wives of the Messenger of Allah had been married before, and Allah Almighty says: *"Indeed in the Messenger of Allah you have a good example for those who hope for Allah and the Last Day."*

> إِن يَكُونُوا۟ فُقَرَآءَ يُغْنِهِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ

A Muslim should answer his Muslim brother who proposes to him, when he is satisfied with the man's religion; and he warned that if this is not done, there will be strife in the land and great corruption. He forbade a marriage sought for other than the face of Allah Almighty and chastity, and he forbade marriage undertaken for show and reputation. He said: "Whoever marries a woman for her standing or her wealth, Allah leaves him to that; but whoever marries her for her religion and her excellence, Allah Almighty grants him beauty and wealth besides." Then he recited the words of Allah Almighty: *"If they should be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is all-Encompassing, Knowing."* And he said: "There is no calamity heavier upon a servant in his religion than that his Muslim kinsman should come to him and say, Marry me your daughter, and he answer, I will not, because he is wealthier than the suitor."

It is told of Ali ibn al-Husayn, (ع), that he passed by a woman in one of the districts of Makkah and was struck by her beauty and character. He inquired about her, found her without a husband, proposed to her, married her, and consummated the marriage. Afterward a man of his kin came to him and said, "O son of the Messenger of Allah, something has weighed upon me concerning your marriage to this woman that I could not bear, for you married her without asking after her lineage. I could not rest until I inquired, and I found her to be of the Banu Shayban, of the noblest of her people, and so I was gladdened and set at ease." Ali ibn al-Husayn said, "And what was it you had feared?" The man said, "I feared she might not be your equal, and that people would speak of it." Ali ibn al-Husayn said to him, "I had thought you of sounder judgment than this. Do you not know that Allah Almighty brought Islam and by it raised the lowly, completed the deficient, and ennobled what was base? There is no reproach upon the affair of a Muslim; reproach belongs only to the Age of Ignorance."

He also married the freedwoman who had borne a son to a man now dead. When Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan heard of it, he wrote reproaching him, thinking he had found in it a fault, and saying, "Was there not enough for you among the women of Quraysh and the noble Arabs to keep you from the mother of another man's son?" Ali ibn al-Husayn wrote back to him: "To proceed: Allah Almighty has by Islam raised the lowly and completed the deficient, so there is no reproach upon the affair of a Muslim; reproach belongs only to the Age of Ignorance. And the Messenger of Allah married such a one," meaning Safiyyah bint Hayy ibn Akhtab, "and in him is a good example." Were it permissible to disdain the mothers of children, the marriage bed would be abandoned and corruption would appear in the land; and the Imams, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), are the most fit to make this plain, that the people might follow their example.

Allah Almighty said: *"O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most honored of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Aware."*

On the day of the conquest of Makkah he addressed the people, praised and glorified Allah, then said: "O people, Allah Almighty has taken from you the arrogance of the Age of Ignorance and its boasting in forefathers. You are all from Adam, and Adam was from clay. The best of Allah's servants before Allah are those most fearful of Him. Arabness is not a thing born of a father; it is a tongue that speaks. Whoever is held back by his deeds, his lineage will not advance him." And every claim of blood or rancor from the Age of Ignorance is beneath his feet until the Day of Resurrection.

It is told that he gave Dubaa bint al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib in marriage to al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and said that he married her to al-Miqdad only that marriage might be made humble, that the people might follow the example of the Messenger of Allah and that they might know that the most honored of them before Allah is the most God-fearing. Al-Zubayr was the brother of Abd Allah, the father of the Prophet, (ع), by both father and mother. Jafar ibn Muhammad said: "The Messenger of Allah married Qurayshi women to freedmen: he gave Dubaa bint al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib to al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and he married Tamim al-Dari to a woman of the Banu Hashim ibn Abd Manaf."

The Messenger of Allah said: "When one whose religion and trustworthiness are pleasing to you comes seeking marriage, then marry him; for if you do not, there will be strife in the earth and great corruption."

It is narrated from Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad that he was in Makkah when word reached him that Dawud ibn Ali had ordered the killing of al-Maali ibn Hunaish, who was one of his own companions, and that he had been killed. Al-Sadiq, (ع), rose in anger, dragging his garment behind him. His son Ismail, (ع), came to meet him and said: "O my father, where are you going? The people are defiant, and their insolence against Allah Almighty is such as you well know. Leave them be." But he struck him upon the chest and said: "Step aside from me. Were it a blazing fire, I would plunge into it." He went on until he came in upon Dawud and said: "O Dawud, you have committed a sin that Allah will never forgive you." Dawud said: "And what is that?" He said: "You have killed a believing man from among the people of Paradise."

Dawud grew angry and fell silent for a time, then said: "And you too have committed a sin that Allah Almighty will not forgive you." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "Your daughter has been given in marriage to a man from Banu Umayyah." Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad answered that in this his example was the Messenger of Allah himself for he had given his daughter Zaynab in marriage to Abu al-As ibn Rabiah, and he had given Umm Kulthum in marriage to Uthman ibn Affan, and when she died he married him to Ruqayyah, both being his daughters and his family.

Then he said: "You are the one who forbade the killing of believers unjustly." Dawud said: "I did not command that he be killed." Al-Sadiq said that al-Sarraqi had reported, "We have lost him," and that he, the killer, had said, "I have taken responsibility for him." So Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad had his companions seize the man and proceed with him to be put to death. The man cried out: "O servants of Allah, do you command me to kill men for them, and then exact retribution from me?" Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad said: "As for you, O enemy of Allah, you confess to the killing, and your companion has denied that he commanded you to it. Have you any proof of that?" The man said: "And who will bear witness for me against Dawud?" He said: "Then retribution from you is obligatory and must be exacted." And he delivered him over to the kinsmen of al-Maali, and they put him to death.

It was said to Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad: Is it permissible to give daughters in marriage to those of opposing views? He answered that the Messenger of Allah had given his daughters in marriage to certain men whom they knew, and that Umar had sought the hand of Ali's daughter Umm Kulthum, (ع), and Ali had refused him. So Umar went to al-Abbas and complained of this to him, and pressed the Banu Abd al-Muttalib hard. Al-Abbas came to Ali, (ع), and said: "O son of my brother, you see the situation we are in. Umar has sought her hand and has pressed us hard over your refusing him." He did not cease until Ali committed her affair to him, and al-Abbas gave her in marriage to Umar on his behalf. It is therefore better to give daughters in marriage to people of sound faith, or to those who do not stir up enmity against the family of the Messenger of Allah and his family. The marriage of a believer is better than the marriage of any other, yet when there is necessity there is no harm in marrying people of differing views from among the Muslims. Likewise to marry among them is not forbidden, as marriage to polytheists is forbidden, but the meritorious and preferred course is marriage among people of sound faith, and after them the weak ones who are neither loyal nor hostile.

> فَإِن طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَن شَىْءٍۢ مِّنْهُ

A man asked Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali about a sister of his wife, a believing woman of knowledge who was in Basra and had no man among her kin to oversee her affair. He said to him: "Do not give her in marriage to them. As for yourselves, there is no harm in your giving the weak women in marriage; but a Nasibiyyah, the daughter of a Nasib, no." Zurara ibn Ayan asked Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad about the like of this, and he was permitted to give the weak women in marriage, but not a Nasibiyyah, the daughter of a Nasib. And Abu Jafar said to Zurara ibn Ayan concerning the weak women: "Keep to the simple and weak among women." And Abu Jafar said: "Marry into the people of doubt, but do not give your women to them in marriage, for a woman takes from her husband's manners, and he prevails over her in the matter of his religion."

He said: "The marriage of people of knowledge, and marriage among them, is foremost and best and nearest to Allah Almighty. If that is not to be had, then the weak ones who are neither loyal nor hostile are better than the people of enmity." After them come the Muslims of the people of truce, whom the Shariah binds together: they marry one another and inherit from one another, and the testimony of one of them concerning another is admissible when they are upright and not suspect. As for the people of disbelief, such as Jews, Christians, and polytheists, it is not lawful for any of them to marry a Muslim woman, though their marrying one another is permissible, and Muslim men may marry their women when there is necessity and Muslim women are not to be found. Muslim women, however, are not lawful for them.

Abu Abd Allah, (ع), was asked about the saying of Allah Almighty: ﴿الزَّانِي لَا يَنْكِحُ إِلَّا زَانِيَةً أَوْ مُشْرِكَةً وَالزَّانِيَةُ لَا يَنْكِحُهَا إِلَّا زَانٍ أَوْ مُشْرِكٌ وَحُرِّمَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, "The adulterer shall not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress shall not marry except an adulterer or a polytheist, and that is forbidden to the believers." He said: "This was revealed concerning women known for licentiousness in the time of ignorance, who were openly hired out for adultery and had set up houses marked for that purpose. The truce came with the provision that whoever wished might return to them; among them were Habibah, al-Rabab, and Sarah, whose blood the Messenger of Allah and his family, declared lawful on the day of the conquest of Makkah, because she had been inciting the polytheists to fight the Messenger of Allah and his family. As for a slave girl who has fallen into fornication, there is no harm in purchasing her and having relations with her, and there is likewise no harm in marrying such a woman when there is necessity, provided one is fortified and guarded against her. Yet chaste women are better and more fitting."

A man came to the Messenger of Allah and his family, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have a woman who does not turn away the hand of one who touches her, and I love her." He said: "Then keep her." It was narrated of a man who saw his wife committing adultery yet was loath to part from her: he may keep her if he wishes. was asked about a man's marrying an immoral woman, and he said: "What prevents him? But if he does so, let him fortify the door of his house." He was asked about a man who marries a slave girl born of adultery, and he said: "There is no harm in it, though to keep clear of that is dearer to me." Concerning a man who has a slave girl who has fallen into fornication, asking whether he may have relations with her, he said: "Yes, if he wishes." Concerning a man who marries a woman without full discernment, he said: "It is permissible, so long as no fault remains attached to his child." Concerning a child of adultery, whether one may have relations with her and sell her if she is a slave girl, and buy her, he said: "Yes; the forbidden does not render the lawful forbidden, nor corrupt it. Were people to turn away from the like of these and forbid their marriage, corruption in the land would multiply, and Allah may yet set right the corrupters and accept the repentance of the sinners."

Some of the Ahl al-Bayt, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), were asked about the saying of Allah Almighty, "The adulterer shall not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist." He said: "The word marry here may mean the act of union and intercourse, or it may mean the contract and marriage. If it means union and intercourse, then it may indeed signify adultery, not lawful marriage." He said: "As for His words, except an adulterer or a polytheist, a man does not bring upon himself the wrath of Allah Almighty in this except while he is a polytheist." And the Messenger of Allah said: "The adulterer does not commit adultery at the moment of his adultery while he is a believer."

**Mentioning the Seeking of Women's Hands in Marriage**

We have narrated from the Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah and upon the Imams of his house, that he forbade a man to propose marriage over the proposal of his brother, and to bid over the bid of his brother. Some of the Ahl al-Bayt explained this and said: The meaning of the words of the Messenger of Allah and his family, that a man should not propose over his brother's proposal, is that this is after there has come about mutual approach, contentment, inclination, attentiveness, and agreement, such that nothing remains but the contract itself. As for what falls short of that, there is no harm in two men, or a group, proposing to a woman until she inclines to one of them and answers him; only then is it disliked for another to oppose him with a proposal. In the same way it is permissible for a man to bid on a commodity and to purchase it, and for another to bid above him, so long as the two parties to the sale have not yet reached agreement.

The Messenger of Allah commanded selling by open auction, and people have continued to this day to outbid one another in the call and otherwise, each raising upon the other until the commodity is settled and the seller accepts a buyer; after that no further bid should be made, nor any raising upon what has been commanded. It is a matter of recommendation, on account of the benefit in it. Should a suitor propose, or a bidder raise his bid upon a commodity, after agreement and before the contract of marriage or sale is concluded, that falls under the same ruling: if one surpasses another in merit before the contract is concluded, it does not invalidate the marriage or the sale, since nothing has become binding to another by contract. And the Messenger of Allah said: "When one of you wishes to marry a woman, let him cast his gaze upon her, for he is but a buyer." And he said: "When one of you wishes to marry a woman, there is no harm in his looking at what draws him to her."

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali said: I mentioned this hadith to Jabir ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari, and he said to me: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah. I sought the hand of a young woman from among the women of the Ansar, and I concealed myself for her behind a wall of her father's garden, and I looked at her and saw what I wished to see and what I had not meant to see, and she pleased me, so I married her, and she was the best of women."

> قُل لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّوا۟ مِنْ أَبْصَرِهِمْ

Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad said: There is no harm for one who wishes to marry a woman in looking at her; but he should not look at a slave girl except with her master's permission, meaning that the master may not wish to sell his slave girl or to offer her. The command from the Messenger of Allah permitting a man to look at the woman he intends to marry, extends the permission of that gaze, once he has come to know that they will give her to him and will not refuse him, when they have agreed and nothing remains but the marriage contract. He should look at her only to acquaint himself with her state, not out of desire to look at her or to take pleasure in her, nor should he deliberately direct his gaze toward her private parts or toward what it is not fitting to look upon. It is not lawful for him to look with the eye of contemplation at women who are not his, that is, women other than his wives, those forbidden to him by blood, and those his right hand possesses, whether they be bareheaded or unveiled, for Allah says, exalted be He, ﴿قُل لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّوا مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِمْ﴾, "Say to the believing men that they lower their gaze."

Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked about a man past whom a woman passes, and he looks at her from behind. He said: "Would it please one of you that men should look upon his womenfolk and his kinswomen? Be content for people with what you are content with for yourselves." And he said concerning the saying of Allah Almighty in the story of Moses, recounting the words of the woman, ﴿قَالَتْ إِحْدَاهُمَا يَا أَبَتِ اسْتَأْجِرْهُ إِنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ اسْتَأْجَرْتَ الْقَوِيُّ الْأَمِينُ﴾, "One of the two women said: O my father, hire him; indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy," that she meant Moses, (ع) and his family. Her father said to her: "As for your saying that he is strong, that is from what you saw of his lifting the rock from the well; but how did you come to know his trustworthiness?" She said: "When he set out with me to come to you, I wished to walk before him to show him the road, but he came forward and said: Walk behind me and direct me to the road, for we are a people who do not look upon the backs of women."

It is narrated from Ali that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah when looking at women was mentioned, and he said: "The first glance is for you," meaning the glance that falls unawares, "and the second is against you, and the third glance is a poisoned arrow from the arrows of Iblis. Whoever forsakes such glances for the sake of Allah Almighty, and for no other, Allah Almighty will requite him with a faith whose sweetness he will taste." And Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad said: "Do those who look upon the forms of women not fear that they may be afflicted with the like in their own wives?"

It is narrated from Ali that a man came to the Messenger of Allah and said: "O Messenger of Allah, should I ask my mother's leave before entering upon her?" He said: "Yes." He said: "And why, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Would it please you to see her unclothed?" He said: "No." He said: "Then ask her leave." He said: "O Messenger of Allah my sister uncovers her hair before me." He said: "No." He said: "Why?" He said: "I fear that, should she reveal one of her charms before you, Satan may invite you toward her." And he said and his family: "When one of you would kiss a woman who is a mahram to him and has come of age, a mother, a sister, an aunt, or any who is forbidden to him in marriage, let him kiss her upon the head and between the eyes, or let him refrain from her cheeks and her mouth."

Concerning Fatimah, (ع): a blind man sought leave to enter upon her, and she veiled herself from him. It was said to her: "He is blind, his sight is wholly gone; he sees nothing of her." She said: "Even if he does not see me, I see him, and he perceives the voice and senses the scent."

The Messenger of Allah asked Ali and a company that was before him, what is best for women, and they did not know what to say. Ali withdrew to Fatimah and mentioned this to her, and she said: "What is best for women is that they should not see men and that men should not see them." Ali went to the Messenger of Allah and said this to him. He said: "Did you arrive at this of yourself, or did another say it?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah it was Fatimah who said it." The Messenger of Allah was pleased by it and said: "Fatimah is but a part of me."

### The Hunt and the Knife: Game, Slaughter, and Sacrifice

The Messenger of Allah taught that whoever desires to marry should not approach the matter heedlessly, but should begin by turning to Allah, praising Him and extolling Him, and then asking Him for the kind of companion that makes a household whole. He said that such a person should pray:

"O Allah, grant me a wife who is affectionate and fruitful, grateful and jealous in her honor. If I do good, she thanks me; if I do wrong, she forgives me; if I remember Allah, she helps me; if I forget, she reminds me; if I go out from her, she guards herself; if I come in to her, she gladdens me; if I command her, she obeys me; if I swear by her, she fulfills my oath; if she becomes angry, You satisfy me. O Lord of majesty and honor, grant me what I have asked for, and what You have apportioned and given."

And he made a clear promise concerning this supplication. The Messenger of Allah said that whoever says these words and acts upon them, Allah Almighty will give him what he has asked.

He also taught that marriage is not a thing to be entered without its proper preliminaries. The Messenger of Allah said that every marriage in which there is no engagement is like a leprous hand.

This same care for the right beginning was kept by his descendants. Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali when he gave a woman in marriage or when a marriage was contracted in his presence, would open with words of praise and witness, saying: "Praise be to Allah. We praise Him and seek refuge with Him from the evils of ourselves and the evils of our deeds. Whoever Allah guides, none can mislead, and whoever He leaves to stray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger."

Then he would recite the words of Allah Almighty:

﴿ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ بِهِ وَالْأَرْحَامَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا ﴾

And he would recite the words of Allah Almighty:

﴿ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنتُم مُّسْلِمُونَ ﴾

And he would recite the words of Allah Almighty:

﴿ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا ۝ يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ أَعْمَالَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ ۚ وَمَن يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ فَازَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا ﴾

Once the marriage has been thus commended and the standing of each party made known to the other, the contract is concluded. The one who performs it praises Allah for what He deserves, prays upon the Prophet ((ع) and his family), recalls the virtue of marriage and what is desired in it, and only then ties the knot. It is fitting that the husband make known to his prospective companion whatever he can of his situation, so that she enters the union with knowledge of his circumstances. And if the contract is not preceded by a formal engagement, it remains permissible, though the khutbah is the better course.

The scholars forbade a formal proposal during the iddah, yet they permitted a discreet hint at marriage, in keeping with the words of Allah Almighty:

﴿ وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُم بِهِ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ النِّسَاءِ أَوْ أَكْنَنتُمْ فِي أَنفُسِكُمْ ۚ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ سَتَذْكُرُونَهُنَّ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا إِلَّا أَن تَقُولُوا قَوْلًا مَّعْرُوفًا ۚ وَلَا تَعْزِمُوا عُقْدَةَ النِّكَاحِ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ الْكِتَابُ أَجَلَهُ ﴾

*There is no blame upon you for what you hint at regarding a proposal to women, or what you conceal within yourselves. Allah knows that you will remember them, but do not make a secret commitment with them except in the form of honorable speech. And do not resolve the marriage contract until the prescribed term reaches its end.* (al-Baqarah: 235)

Jafar ibn Muhammad said concerning the words of Allah Almighty, "do not make a secret commitment with them": this refers to a secret pledge of marriage, while exposing them gently to the matter and speaking goodly words is the permitted hinting at the khutbah.

It was narrated from Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali that he entered upon Sakina bint Handhalah, who had been separated from a cousin of hers who had married her and then died. Abu Jafar greeted her and said, "How have you been, O daughter of Handhalah?" She said, "May I be your ransom, O son of the Messenger of Allah." He said, "You know my kinship to the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family), and my standing with Ali, and my right in Islam, and my honor among the Arabs." She said, "May Allah forgive you, O Abu Jafar. You propose to me while I am in my iddah!" He said, "I have done no such thing. I have only informed you of my status and my standing. The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) once entered upon Umm Salamah, the daughter of Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumiyyah, while she was in her iddah from Abu Salamah, who was her cousin. He continued to mention his standing to her until the impression of the mat showed upon his palm from the force with which he leaned upon his hand, and yet that was not a formal proposal." They said: it is recommended for one who wishes to marry to acquaint his prospective companion with his situation, so that she may know his circumstances.

It was related that when the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) proposed to her, Umm Salamah (رض) sent word to him saying, "O Messenger of Allah, I am an elderly woman, I have children, and I am a woman of great jealousy, and I fear there may be something in me of which you are unaware." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent back to her, "As for your age, you have mentioned it, and I am older than you. As for your children, they shall be among the children of the Messenger of Allah. And as for your jealousy, I shall pray to Allah Almighty to remove it from you." And he married her ((ع) and his family).

**The Wedding Feast and the Consummation of Marriage**

We have narrated from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah (may the prayers of Allah be upon him and upon his family and upon them all) that the feast is of four kinds: the walimah, the khurs, the idhar, and the wakirah. The walimah is the food prepared when a man enters upon his wife. The khurs is the food of the aqiqah prepared for the newborn on the seventh day, which has already been mentioned along with what is obligatory in it. The idhar is the food prepared at the circumcision of a boy. The wakirah is when a man returns from a journey, prepares food, and invites people to it. He said ((ع) and his family): it is among the Sunnah of the Messengers to provide food upon marriage. The Prophet ((ع) and his family) held a wedding feast for his wives when he consummated marriage with them, and at some of his feasts he served al-hays, a food made of dates, ghee, and condensed milk. He said to one of his companions who had married, "Give a feast, even if it be only with a sheep." And he said ((ع) and his family), "The feast of the first day is a duty, the feast of the second day is a kindness known among people, and what is beyond that is ostentation and reputation-seeking." Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad (may the prayers of Allah be upon them) was invited to a feast on the first day and he answered it; he was invited on the second day and he answered it; then a messenger came to him on the third day to invite him, and he ordered the messenger turned away until he was out of sight.

It was narrated from the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) that he passed by Banu Zurayq and heard the sound of instruments and singing, and he asked, "What is this?" They said, "O Messenger of Allah, so-and-so has married so-and-so." He said, "He has completed his religion. This is marriage, not a clandestine affair, and there is no marriage in secret, until its smoke is seen and the sound of the tambourine is heard." And he said ((ع) and his family), "What distinguishes marriage from fornication is the beating of the tambourine." It was also narrated from him ((ع) and his family) that on the night Fatimah was brought to Ali he heard the beat of the tambourine, and he asked, "What is this?" Umm Salamah said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is Asma bint Umays beating the tambourine for Fatimah, lest she say within herself, My mother has died and there is no one to rejoice with me." The Messenger of Allah raised his hands to the heavens and said, "O Allah, bring joy to Asma bint Umays as she has gladdened the daughter of Your Prophet." Then he called her and said, "O Asma, what do you say when you beat the tambourine?" She said, "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah I do not know what to say; I only wished to gladden her." He said, "Then do not say anything indecent, but say: We have come to you, we have come to you; so greet us and we will greet you."

This kind of speech and its like, together with the beating of the tambourine and what resembles it, is what permission has been granted for at weddings and banquets. As for other speech that carries vulgarity, and the singing that accompanies it, and the instruments of diversion and the entrancing flutes that the people of frivolity take up, that is disliked.

Al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked about such things, and he recited the words of Allah Almighty:

﴿ وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاءَ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَاعِبِينَ ۝ لَوْ أَرَدْنَا أَن نَّتَّخِذَ لَهْوًا لَّاتَّخَذْنَاهُ مِن لَّدُنَّا إِن كُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ ۝ بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِالْحَقِّ عَلَى الْبَاطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُ فَإِذَا هُوَ زَاهِقٌ ۚ وَلَكُمُ الْوَيْلُ مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ ﴾

*We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play. Had We intended to take a pastime, We would have taken it from near Us, were We to do so. Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and at once it vanishes. And woe to you for what you describe.* (al-Anbiya: 16–18)

It was narrated from him that he said, "Singing is a gathering upon which Allah Almighty does not look." It was narrated from him that he was asked about the flute, and he said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: there are two voices that Allah Almighty detests: a wailing at the time of calamity, and a flute at the time of blessing." And it was narrated from him regarding the words of Allah Almighty:

﴿ فَاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الْأَوْثَانِ وَاجْتَنِبُوا قَوْلَ الزُّورِ ﴾

*So avoid the abomination of idols, and avoid the false statement* (al-Hajj: 30)

> وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشْتَرِى لَهْوَ ٱلْحَدِيثِ

that "the abomination of idols" includes chess, and that "the false statement" includes singing. He said concerning the words of Allah Almighty, ﴿ وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَن يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ ﴾ *And among the people is he who purchases idle talk* (Luqman: 6), that this too refers to singing.

One of his companions said, "I was in Madinah and came upon a place where there was singing, so I sat and listened. The next day I entered upon Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad, and when I sat before him he began by reciting the words of Allah, exalted be His mention:

﴿ إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُولَٰئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا ﴾

*Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart: about all those one will be questioned.* (al-Isra: 36)

Then he looked at me and said, You will be asked of your hearing what it heard, of your heart what it understood, and of your sight what it beheld."

It was narrated from him that he said, "The sale of singing is not lawful, nor its purchase; listening to it is hypocrisy, and teaching it is disbelief." It was also narrated from him that one day some of his Shia, who had come as a delegation from various towns, entered upon him, and he asked them, "Where have you lodged?" They said, "O son of the Messenger of Allah, we lodged in a house, and when we drew near to the place we heard singing within it, so we sought another lodging but could not find one." He said, "Even so, be noble: keep your hearing far from listening to it and lending it your ear, for Allah, exalted is the One who speaks, says:

﴿ وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ وَإِذَا مَرُّوا بِاللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا كِرَامًا ﴾

*And those who do not bear witness to falsehood, and when they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity.* (al-Furqan: 72)"

It was narrated from him that he said, "My father passed by me one day when I was a boy, and I had stopped to listen to two pipers. He took me by the hand and said, Step away; do not be of those who gloated over Adam (ع). I said, How is that, O my father? He said, All the amusement, play, and singing that you see was devised by Iblis to gloat over Adam when he was expelled from Paradise." He said, "The house in which singing takes place is a house in which no calamity is met with comfort, no supplication is answered, and the angel does not enter." It was narrated from him that he said, "Singing causes hypocrisy to grow in the heart as water causes the date palm to bring forth its spathe." And it was narrated from him that he said, "Whoever has the lute played in his house for forty days, Allah sets over him a devil called al-Anqad, who leaves no limb of his without sitting upon it; and when he is thus afflicted, his sense of shame is stripped from him, and he no longer cares what he says or what is said to him."

> وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشْتَرِى لَهْوَ ٱلْحَدِيثِ

It was mentioned to him that a man of his Shia had entered upon someone he knew, and that man brought out a slave-girl of his who played and sang, and she sang and played before him. Jafar ibn Muhammad said, "Did he not fear that the command of Allah Almighty might come upon him while he was in such a state, in a gathering upon which Allah does not look?" It was also narrated from him that a man asked him about singing, and he said to him, "Tell me: if Allah Almighty separates truth from falsehood, where do you see singing falling?" The man said, "O son of the Messenger of Allah, I see it only with falsehood." He said, "Then I reckon you have judged it. Leave it, for there is no good in it, and it is among that for which Allah Almighty has promised the Fire." Then he recited the words of Allah Almighty, ﴿ وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَن يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ ﴾ *And among the people is he who purchases idle talk* (Luqman: 6). It was also narrated from him that singing bequeaths hypocrisy and brings on poverty.

And he said that the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) forbade his community al-zafn, the flute, the drums, and the reed-pipes; and that a man who had broken a lute was once brought before Ali, and Ali approved his deed and ruled that there was no liability for breaking the lute. All of this points to the prohibition of frivolity and of listening to singing, flutes, lyres, and the like that are taken up for diversion. As for what is used in war, in the marshaling and parading of troops, and the like, such as what people raise up before the Imams and the commanders of armies by beating drums and shields and by blowing horns and pipes that are not taken for enjoyment and amusement, that is not among what was forbidden, nor of the kind whose prohibition has just been mentioned. Rather it is among what is recommended in its proper place. For it has come from the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) that he passed by a company of Abyssinians beating their drums, and he said, "Carry on, O sons of Arfidah, that the Jews may know there is breadth in our religion."

If someone should ask, "Why then do we hear and see, in the lands where the Imams hold authority (may the prayers of Allah be upon them), the very instruments of diversion that they have forbidden?" the answer is that this is no greater than the indecencies that Allah Almighty has forbidden and made unlawful, which people nonetheless commit in their homes, behind their doors and their curtains. Allah has commanded that the prescribed penalties be carried out for those indecencies upon which He has commanded such penalties, in what appears openly and is witnessed by witnesses. As for what remains hidden, He alone, glorified be He, holds the knowledge of it and has reserved to Himself both its punishment and its pardon, advancing of that what He wills and deferring what He defers. It is well known and widely established among all people that the Imams denounced these things upon those who did them and withheld any license for them, holding that this is not a matter for which the hadd is due, but rather one calling for denunciation and prohibition.

It was narrated from the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) that he said, "Bring your brides in by night, and give the feast by day." And it was narrated from him that he said, "There is no staying awake save in three: a vigil with the Quran, the seeking of knowledge, or the bringing of a bride to her husband." It was also narrated from him that a man should make himself ready for his wife as he would wish her to make herself ready for him; Jafar ibn Muhammad said that this means cleanliness.

He said: when a man's wife is brought to him and she enters upon him, let him pray two rakahs, then place his hand upon her forelock and say, "O Allah, bless me in my wife and bless her in me; in whatever You have joined between us, join us in goodness, felicity, and blessing; and if You decree a parting, make it a parting toward every good." Then, when he sits beside her, let him wipe her forelock and say, "Praise be to Allah, who guided my straying, enriched my poverty, raised up my burden, gave might to my lowliness, sheltered my dependents, gave a spouse to my solitude, bore up my step, served my need, brought company to my loneliness, and lifted my standing; a praise wholesome, abundant, and blessed, for what You have granted, O Lord, and for what You have apportioned, and for what You have honored."

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali said: the woman too is commanded to be in a state of ablution on the night she is brought as a bride; when her husband prays, she prays, and when he supplicates, she says amen. He added that one should increase in supplication, sending prayers upon the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) at the beginning, the middle, and the end, and saying within it, "O Allah, grant me her affection, her warmth, her contentment with me and my contentment with her, and join us in the best of unions and the gentlest of bonds, for You love the lawful and hate the unlawful."

And Jafar ibn Muhammad said: when a man wishes to come to his wife, let him say, "O Allah, if You decree from me this day a child, then make him purely Yours, and grant the devil no share in him, no portion and no part; indeed You are powerful over all things." It was narrated from the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) that he said, "When one of you comes to his wife, let him not hasten her," and that when he is with her, let him deal kindly and truly with her. And he ((ع) and his family) forbade that a man be intimate with a free woman while another woman is in the room with her. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali said there is no harm in that with a bondwoman, and likewise said Jafar ibn Muhammad. And it was narrated from Ali that he said it does not befit a man to be intimate with his wife

Jafar ibn Muhammad said that when a man wishes to come to his wife, let him say: «اَللَّهُمَّ إِنْ قَضَيْتَ مِنِّي الْيَوْمَ خَلْقًا فَاجْعَلْهُ لَكَ خَالِصًا، وَلَا تَجْعَلْ لِلشَّيْطَانِ فِيهِ شِرْكًا وَلَا حَظًّا وَلَا نَصِيبًا، إِنَّكَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ» "O Allah, if You decree from me today a creation, make it purely for You, and grant the devil in it no share, no portion, and no part, for You are able to do all things." And from the Messenger of Allah and his family, it was related that he said: «إِذَا أَتَىٰ أَحَدُكُمُ امْرَأَتَهُ فَلَا يُعْجِلْهَا، وَإِذَا وَاقَعَهَا فَلْيَصْدُقْهَا» "When one of you comes to his wife, let him not hasten her, and when he is with her, let him deal truthfully with her."

He and his family, permitted a man to come to a free wife while another wife is present in the house. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him, said there is no objection to this in the case of a bondwoman, and likewise said Jafar ibn Muhammad. From Ali it was related that a man should not come to his wife while facing the qibla. He also said that to gaze during intercourse brings on blindness. The Prophet and his family, and the Imams of his progeny, would turn the face away from any animal being mounted upon the road, and he would avert his face.

He named a hidden form of infanticide, الْوَأْدُ الْخَفِيُّ: that a man comes to a woman, and when he senses the issuing of the fluid he withdraws from her and spills it elsewhere. Of this he said, "So do not do that." He said that the Messenger of Allah and his family, forbade withdrawal from a free woman except with her leave, and from a bondwoman taken in marriage except with the leave of her master. Ali said that a man may withdraw from his own bondwoman as he wishes, and likewise said Jafar ibn Muhammad.

From Ali by way of Jafar ibn Muhammad: a man should not lie between two free women, though he may lie between two bondwomen; and he should not look upon the awrah of a free woman, nor expose his own awrah to her. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali said that intercourse is disliked from the breaking of dawn until sunrise, and from the setting of the sun until the fading of twilight; and on the night in which the moon is eclipsed, and on the day in which the sun is eclipsed; and on the day and night in which the earth quakes; and when the yellow, the black, and the red winds blow.

He said: The Messenger of Allah and his family, passed a night with one of his wives on a night in which the moon was eclipsed, and nothing passed between him and her. It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is this coldness?" He said, "It is no coldness, but this was a sign, and I was loath to take my pleasure on such a night, that I might not be among those whom Allah, mighty and majestic, has rebuked in His Book where He says: «وَإِن يَرَوْا كِسْفًا مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ سَاقِطًا يَقُولُوا سَحَابٌ مَّرْكُومٌ» And were they to see a fragment falling from the sky, they would say: a heaped-up cloud." Then Abu Jafar, may Allah's blessings be upon him, said: By Him who sent Muhammad with prophethood, singled him out with the message, and honored him with nobility, none of you comes to his wife at any of these disliked times and is then granted offspring in whom he sees the delight of his eye.

From Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him: a slave girl under nine years of age is not to be approached; if a man does so and she is harmed by it, he is liable. Jafar ibn Muhammad, may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family, said: If a man marries a young girl, he does not enter upon her until she completes nine years from the day of her birth.

From Ali, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, it was related that he disliked the coming to women in their hinder parts, and he used to forbid it, citing the words of Allah, mighty and majestic, that one may come to them only «فِي الْفُرُوجِ مِنْ قُبُلٍ أَوْ دُبُرٍ» in the place of tilth, whether from before or from behind. And from the Messenger of Allah and his family, it was related that he said: «لَا يَخْلُو رَجُلٌ بِامْرَأَةٍ غَيْرِ ذَاتِ مَحْرَمٍ مِنْهُ إِلَّا كَانَ الشَّيْطَانُ ثَالِثَهُمَا» "No man is alone with a woman who is not his mahram but that the devil is the third of them." He forbade conversing with women other than one's wives and one's mahrams. Jafar ibn Muhammad, may Allah's blessings be upon him, said: «حَدِيثُ النِّسَاءِ يُورِثُ النِّسْيَانَ وَيُزِيغُ الْقَلْبَ وَهُوَ مِنْ مَصَائِدِ الشَّيْطَانِ» "Idle talk with women breeds forgetfulness and makes the heart swerve, and it is among the snares of the devil."

> فَإِن طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَن شَىْءٍۢ مِّنْهُ

The Messenger of Allah and his family, said: «اِتَّقُوا اللَّهَ فِي النِّسَاءِ، فَإِنَّهُنَّ عِيٌّ وَعَوْرَةٌ، وَإِنَّكُمُ اسْتَحْلَلْتُمُوهُنَّ بِأَمَانَةِ اللَّهِ» "Fear Allah concerning women, for they are weak of speech and are a thing to be covered, and you have made them lawful to you by the trust of Allah." He said: They have their weakness, so treat their weakness with restraint of speech, and shelter that which is to be covered within the homes; do not lodge them in the upper rooms, do not teach them to write, but teach them Surat al-Nur. And from him and his family, he said: «نِعْمَ شُغْلُ الْمَرْأَةِ الْمُؤْمِنَةِ الْمِغْزَلُ» "How excellent an occupation for a believing woman is the spindle." From him also and his family, when he took the pledge from women he would take upon them that they would not speak with men other than their husbands and their mahrams.

It was related from him and his family, that he forbade women to look upon men, and that a woman should not leave her house without her husband's leave, not even for the bath save out of necessity. And it was related that he said one day to his companions, "What is the woman?" They said, "An awrah, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "Yes." Then he said, "And when is she nearest to her Lord?" They had no answer to give. Ali mentioned this to Fatimah, may Allah's blessings be upon her, and she said, "Return to him and say: O Messenger of Allah, the nearest a woman is to her Lord is when she keeps to the innermost of her house." He went and informed the Prophet and his family, who said, "This is from you, O Ali." He said, "No, O Messenger of Allah, rather it was Fatimah who said it." The Messenger of Allah and his family, said, "She has spoken truly; «إِنَّهَا بِضْعَةٌ مِنِّي» indeed she is a part of me."

From the Messenger of Allah and his family: he forbade a woman to walk unclothed before her husband, and forbade the man to be unclothed before her. He forbade women to comb their hair with wine or to apply its dregs, and he forbade women to imitate men and men to imitate women, and he cursed whoever did so. From him: "Any woman who perfumes herself, let her not leave her house, nor attend the prayer with us." And from him: he forbade women, when they go out behind men, to walk in the middle of the road with them, and he said, "Women have no portion of the middle of the road." He forbade that a woman should wear, when she goes out, a garment that draws notice, or adorn herself with what makes a sound, or strike with her foot so that the chime of her anklet is heard. He forbade women from open display, from wailing, and from raising the voice except out of necessity, and from conversing with men, and from passing the night away from their homes.

He forbade the giving of greeting to women. And from him, may Allah's blessings be upon him, he said that a man should not touch a man unless there is a garment between them, nor a woman a woman unless there is a garment between them. From him and his family: a woman came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have a husband who is harsh of nature, and I have worked something to turn his affection toward me." The Messenger of Allah said to her, "Fie upon you! You have sullied your religion, and the angels of heaven and the angels of earth have cursed you." From him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: «لَوْ كُنْتُ آمِرًا أَحَدًا أَنْ يَسْجُدَ لِأَحَدٍ لَأَمَرْتُ الْمَرْأَةَ أَنْ تَسْجُدَ لِزَوْجِهَا» "Had I been commanding anyone to prostrate to another, I would have commanded the woman to prostrate to her husband." He forbade a woman to deny her husband herself when he called her, and to deny him her help and her work. He said, "The best thing with which a woman adorns herself is the fear of Allah and obedience to her husband."

He said and his family: When a woman knows her Lord and believes in Him and in His Messenger, and acknowledges the merit of the People of the House of her Prophet, and prays the five prayers, and fasts the month of Ramadan, and guards her chastity, and obeys her husband, she enters by whichever of the gates of Paradise she wishes. From him: a woman sent to him saying, "O Messenger of Allah, my husband has ordered me not to go out, near or far, until he returns from his journey; and my father is in the market. Shall I go out to him?" The Messenger of Allah said to her, "Sit in your house and obey your husband." So she did, and her father died. The Messenger of Allah and his family, sent to her saying, "Truly Allah, mighty and majestic, has forgiven your father on account of your obedience to your husband."

A woman asked him, may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of the husband over the wife?" He said, "She must not give in charity from his house except by his leave, nor deny him herself even upon the saddle's back, nor fast a voluntary day except by his leave, nor leave her house except by his leave; and if she goes out without his leave, the angels of heaven, the angels of earth, the angels of mercy, and the angels of wrath curse her until she returns." She said, "O Messenger of Allah, who has the greatest right over a man?" He said, "His parents." "And who has the greatest right over a woman?" He said, "Her husband." She said, "O Messenger of Allah, then have I no right over him to match what he has over me?" He said, "No, not even one in a hundred." And it was related that he assigned to his daughter Fatimah, may Allah's blessings be upon her, the service of what was within the house, and assigned to Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him, the service of what was outside it.

Jafar ibn Muhammad, may Allah's blessings be upon him, was asked about the right of the woman over her husband, the fulfilling of which makes him a doer of good. He said: He feeds her and clothes her, and when she wrongs him he pardons her. He said: My father, may Allah's blessings be upon him, had a wife who used to vex him, and he would forgive her and would say: The Messenger of Allah and his family, said: «اَلْمَرْأَةُ كَالضِّلَعِ، إِنْ تَرَكْتَهَا اِنْتَفَعْتَ بِهَا، وَإِنْ أَقَمْتَهَا كَسَرْتَهَا» "The woman is like a rib: if you leave it be, you take benefit from it, and if you try to straighten it, you break it." It was said to him, "But the woman is jealous over her husband." He said, "That is love."

He was asked about a man who turns away from his wife because worship, fasting, and prayer occupy him from her. He said: The wife of Uthman ibn Mazun came to the Messenger of Allah and said, "O Messenger of Allah, Uthman fasts the day and stands the night in prayer." He understood and his family, what she intended, and he went out to the mosque, where he found Uthman ibn Mazun standing in prayer, and he said, "O Uthman, Allah, mighty and majestic, did not send me with monasticism; He sent me with the upright way. Whoever loves my nature, let him follow my Sunnah, and among my Sunnah is marriage." And the Messenger of Allah and his family, forbade the striking of women where it is not warranted.

From Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him: a man of the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah and his family, with his daughter and said, "O Messenger of Allah, her husband has struck her; grant her retaliation against him." The Messenger of Allah and his family, granted her that. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, sent down: «الرِّجَالُ قَوَّامُونَ عَلَى النِّسَاءِ بِمَا فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ وَبِمَا أَنفَقُوا مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ ۚ فَالصَّالِحَاتُ قَانِتَاتٌ حَافِظَاتٌ لِّلْغَيْبِ بِمَا حَفِظَ اللَّهُ ۚ وَاللَّاتِي تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ فَعِظُوهُنَّ وَاهْجُرُوهُنَّ فِي الْمَضَاجِعِ وَاضْرِبُوهُنَّ ۖ فَإِنْ أَطَعْنَكُمْ فَلَا تَبْغُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ سَبِيلًا ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيًّا كَبِيرًا» "Men are the protectors and maintainers of women, because Allah has favored some of them over others, and because they spend of their wealth. So the righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in the husband's absence what Allah would have them guard. As for those from whom you fear discord, admonish them, then leave them apart in their beds, then strike them. But if they obey you, seek no way against them. Surely Allah is Most High, Most Great." (al-Nisa: 34) And the Messenger of Allah then said: «أَرَدْتُ أَمْرًا وَأَرَادَ اللَّهُ غَيْرَهُ» "I intended one thing, and Allah intended another."

From him he said that jealousy is a part of faith, and a careless yielding is a part of hypocrisy, meaning jealousy in what is forbidden, and the yielding that brings men and women together for that. In another report from Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him, the Messenger of Allah and his family, forbade al-madhal, which is the abandonment of due jealousy. Its root is from a man's making known his secret, that is, exposing it, and from this is taken a man's exposing of his womenfolk to other men. As for jealousy in what is lawful, it is disliked and forbidden. Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him, said: There is no jealousy in the lawful, in light of the saying of the Messenger of Allah and his family, on the night he brought Fatimah, may Allah's blessings be upon her, in to her husband, after she had come to be his: «لَا تُحْدِثَا شَيْئًا حَتَّىٰ آتِيَكُمَا» "Do not do anything until I come to you." He said this to them after they had lain down. So Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him, held back, and the Messenger of Allah and his family, entered and prayed for them and blessed them, and then departed.

From the Messenger of Allah and his family, he said: «كُتِبَ الْجِهَادُ عَلَىٰ رِجَالِ أُمَّتِي وَالْغَيْرَةُ عَلَىٰ نِسَائِهَا، فَمَنْ صَبَرَتْ مِنْهُنَّ وَاحْتَسَبَتْ أَعْطَاهَا اللَّهُ أَجْرَ شَهِيدٍ» "Striving has been prescribed upon the men of my community, and jealousy upon its women; so whichever of them is patient and seeks her reward, Allah, mighty and majestic, grants her the reward of a martyr." From him he mentioned women and what they ask of men, and said: They burden men, when they deck themselves in gold and wear silk; they burden the rich and wear out the poor. And from Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him, he said: Whoever obeys his wife in four things, Allah casts him upon his face into the Fire: that he obey her in going to wedding feasts, to gatherings of wailing, to visitings, and to the bathhouses.

**On Marriage Through Guardians**

We have related from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah and his family: «لَا نِكَاحَ إِلَّا بِوَلِيٍّ وَشَاهِدَيْ عَدْلٍ» "There is no marriage save with a guardian and two upright witnesses." And he forbade that a woman be given in marriage until she is consulted. From Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him, he said: None of you should give his daughter in marriage until he consults her, for she knows best her own self; if she keeps silent, or weeps, or laughs, that is her leave, and if she refuses, he does not marry her off. The arranging by fathers of the marriage of their minor sons and daughters is permissible, and they have no right of dissolution when they come of age; and when an agent is authorized to contract a marriage, it is valid. From him, may Allah's blessings be upon him, he said: If a Muslim woman, being of age, authorizes her Christian father to give her in marriage, and he does so, the marriage is valid; but if he gives her in marriage while she is a child, it is not valid, for a disbeliever has no guardianship over a Muslim.

When a woman entrusts two guardians and delegates the matter to both of them, and each of them marries her to a different man, the marriage belongs to the first of the two, provided that the first was unaware of the other's contract. If the two contracts are concluded at one and the same time, one of them is annulled and the matter is begun anew thereafter. From Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali and from Jafar ibn Muhammad it is related that they said: A paternal grandfather may contract the marriage of his son's minor daughter just as the father contracts it, and he has the prior right in this, even if the two of them should contract at the same moment. All of them are bound by the first contract concluded among them, even if the one whose contract is dissolved was unaware of the other and only learns of it afterward, in which case the matter is resumed.

From Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali it is related that he said: Whatever testimony is admissible in financial matters is admissible in marriage, and the testimony of women and of slaves is accepted in it. From Jafar ibn Muhammad: He was asked about two witnesses who testified in the marriage of a woman that her father had given her in marriage while she was unwilling, and another witness testified that he had given her in marriage with her consent. He said: The marriage is valid with her consent. He was also asked about two witnesses, one of whom testified that the dowry was one thousand and the other that it was two thousand. He said: If she claims the greater amount, she takes an oath together with her witness, and it is decreed for her. If one of them testifies that her father gave her in marriage while she was a child, and the other testifies that he gave her in marriage when she was of age and without her consent, the testimony is void.

**Mentioning the Witnesses in Marriage**

I have mentioned in what came before this chapter that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: There is no marriage save with a guardian and two witnesses. This is what is commanded, and upon it action is taken, and by it the marriage is established. It is related from Ali that he said: A marriage is not valid except with a guardian and witnesses. Abu Jafar and Abu Abdullah, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), said: Witnesses were appointed in marriage only for the sake of the child, so that it may be known who his father is, and as a safeguard against either of the spouses denying the marriage, and out of caution before the authorities, lest the two be charged with being a man and a woman united unlawfully. For this reason, and for whatever resembles it, the seeking of witnesses in marriage is obligatory. As for what lies between a person and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there is nothing upon him if he does not call witnesses, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned witnessing only in the matter of divorce and did not mention it in the matter of marriage. Yet witnesses in marriage cannot be dispensed with, because through them the marriage is established, lineage is confirmed, and doubt is removed, and upright persons bear witness to it. Among the witnesses, women and slaves are admissible, provided they are upright.

**Mentioning the Dowries**

We narrate concerning the Commander of the Believers, (ع). Allah, exalted be the One who speaks, said: ﴿ وَآتُوا النِّسَاءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةً ﴾. Ali said concerning the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿ وَآتُوا النِّسَاءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةً ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is saying, give them the gift by which you have made their private parts lawful to you. So whoever wrongs a woman in her dowry has made her private part lawful to himself through fornication. And the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forgives every sin save the sin of a man who has defrauded a hired laborer of his wage, or a woman of her dowry, or who has sold a free person.

It is related from him that he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, did not marry any of his wives, nor did he give any of his daughters in marriage, for more than twelve uqiyyahs and a nashsh of silver. An uqiyyah is forty dirhams, and a nashsh is half an uqiyyah, so that is five hundred dirhams in all, together with a woven cloak and a bed of ram's hide. This is the dowry of the Sunnah. There is no fixed limit set upon dowries, and whatever is named, be it little or much, the marriage is contracted upon it. It is recommended that it be made easy. Ali said: Among the blessings of a woman is the ease of her marriage and the ease of her womb, so do not be excessive in the dowries of women, for that breeds enmity.

He said: A man came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family, and said: O Messenger of Allah, I wish to marry a certain woman. He said: Do you have anything to give her?
