The man said: No, by Allah, I have nothing. So he looked at a ring upon his hand and said: This ring that is on your hand. The man said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: Then you have married her with this ring of yours. So ease in marriage is a merit, as has been related, and there is no harm in going beyond it either. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿ وَآتَيْتُمْ إِحْدَاهُنَّ قِنطَارًا فَلَا تَأْخُذُوا مِنْهُ شَيْئًا ﴾. And it has come down from al-Husayn ibn Ali both, that he married a woman and sent to her one hundred slave girls, with each slave girl a thousand dirhams.

We have narrated from Abu Abdullah that he was asked about the dowry, and he said: It is whatever the two spouses agree upon, be it little or much. But a dowry there must be, and no marriage is permissible without a dowry, though there is no harm in contracting it without one being named, and he may not consummate it until he gives her something, whatever it may be. This is for the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ لَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِن طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ مَا لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ أَوْ تَفْرِضُوا لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً ﴾. So a contract without a named dowry is, on this basis, permissible, but he may not consummate it until he gives her something. Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked about this and said: My father married a woman and did not name a dowry for her, and when he wished to consummate the marriage he took a garment from me and handed it to her.

He was asked about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ وَامْرَأَةً مُؤْمِنَةً إِن وَهَبَتْ نَفْسَهَا لِلنَّبِيِّ ﴾. He said: That is something singled out for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. No marriage is sound except with a dowry. If he does not name a dowry for her and then dies before her, or divorces her before consummating the marriage, she has no dowry, yet he inherits from her and she from him, and she must observe the waiting period. If he has consummated the marriage, she is entitled to the like of the dowry of the women of her family, according to her condition, her wealth, and her beauty, measured against one of his like in condition and in wealth, provided that this does not exceed the dowry of the Sunnah. If it does exceed it, the excess is returned to him, and the dowry of the Sunnah, as we have mentioned, is five hundred dirhams.

It is related from him concerning a man who married a woman upon her own determination, that he said: The marriage is valid; and if the two disagree as to the amount of the dowry, she is entitled to the like of the dowry of the women of her family, neither falling short nor going to excess, and it is not permissible for it to exceed the dowry of the Sunnah.

It is related from him that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, forbade the marriage of exchange. Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad said: The marriage of exchange, shighar, is that a man give his daughter in marriage to another man on the condition that the other give him his daughter in marriage, with no dowry between them. He said: Two men came to Ali and each married the other's daughter without a dowry, so he rejected it and said: No, there must be a dowry. This applies when the contract in such a marriage is made on the basis that the marriage of the one is in return for the marriage of the other, each being set as the recompense for the other, and they oblige themselves to this. But if they contract it as a marriage is contracted without a named dowry, and do not stipulate within it what we have described, then the contract is valid, and each of the two women is entitled to the like of the dowry of the women of her family, in the manner we have described.

They permitted the contracting of marriage upon described and known goods. They narrated from Ali that he said concerning a man who married a woman in return for a young servant: neither falling short nor going to excess. Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad said: Whoever marries a woman for an unknown dowry has not thereby corrupted the marriage; she is entitled to the like of the dowry of her peers, and it shall be no more than the dowry of the Sunnah.

He was asked about a man who married a woman in return for a slave girl of his who had been pledged her freedom upon his death, and who then divorced her before consummating the marriage. He said: The woman is entitled to half the service of the pledged slave girl, so that the woman has one day of her service and her master one day; and if the master revokes the pledge of freedom or sells her, the woman is entitled to half her value. They said: The dowry belongs to the woman. They narrated from Ali that he said: Marriage in return for a wage paid to the father is not lawful in Islam, in the manner that Moses hired himself out. The dowry belongs only to the wife. If a man marries a woman on the condition that he perform some work for her, the marriage is valid, and the wage in that case stands in place of the dowry; he may not consummate the marriage until he has done for her the work for which he was engaged, or has given her something.

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali said: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, and said: O Messenger of Allah, give me in marriage. He said: Who will take this woman? A man among the people said: I, O Messenger of Allah. He said: What will you give her? He said: I have no wealth. He said: With no wealth at all? So the woman turned to go. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, repeated his words, and no one rose but that man, and the woman turned away again. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said to the man a third time: Do you know anything of the Quran? He said: Yes. He said: I have given her to you in marriage for what you know of the Quran. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali said: If a man marries a woman on the condition that he teach her a chapter from the Book of Allah, I would not have him consummate the marriage until he has taught her or given her something.

From Ali it is related that he said: Once a woman has been brought in to her husband, she has no claim to her dowry after she has entered upon him except by clear proof, meaning, if she claims that he gave her nothing and that something of her dowry remains owing to her. Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad said: If he marries her with a portion paid at once and a portion deferred, the immediate portion falls due before consummation, and he may not consummate the marriage if she withholds herself from him until he pays it to her. The deferred portion runs until death or separation, that is, when no time of payment has been stipulated upon him. But if she stipulates that it become due after consummation, it has been related from Ali that a woman brought before him a man who had married her, consummated the marriage, and named a term for her dowry, and Ali said: There is no term for you in her dowry once you have consummated the marriage; her right has fallen due, so pay her her right. This, and Allah knows best, is when he had paid her nothing in advance, or had named for her neither an immediate nor a deferred portion. But if he named that and paid her at once what he had obligated upon himself, then the deferred remainder runs to the time he stipulated, for the words of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace: People are bound by their conditions. Likewise, if he named no term but named a dowry for her, and she refused that he consummate the marriage until he discharge it, that is her right.

From Ali it is related that he said concerning a man who marries a woman and witnesses are called secretly the first time upon one dowry and openly another time upon a greater dowry: the first is the marriage contract, and by it the matter is taken. From him that he said: When the curtains are let down and the doors are shut, the dowry has fallen due. This is the saying of Abu Jafar and Abu Abdullah and that is when the woman claims that the union took place. But if she acknowledges that he did not touch her, even though he had let down his curtain and shut his door upon them, and he then divorces her, she is entitled to no more than half the dowry, and she must observe the waiting period, for the waiting period is not waived from her by her claim that he did not touch her once he has shut his door and let down his curtain over her.

From Ali and Abu Jafar and Abu Abdullah it is related that they said concerning a man who makes the freeing of his slave woman her dowry: that this is permissible. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali said: That is when the condition is set before the freeing, that is, he says: I marry you on the condition that I have made your dowry your freedom, and then he frees her. But if he frees her first and says to her: I free you for the sake of Allah on the condition that your freedom is your dowry and I marry you upon that, then the choice is hers: if she wishes she marries him, and if she wishes she does not, because she has been freed and has come to own herself apart from him. If he marries her after that, let him marry her with a dowry.

From Ali it is related that he was asked about a man who steals wealth and marries with it, or buys a slave girl with it. He said: The union is lawful, but the liability for the wealth remains upon him, and he is a sinner for what he has done, and he must make restitution for what he stole.

**Mentioning the Conditions in Marriage**

We have narrated from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, and from the Imams of his household, that he said: Every condition that contradicts the Book of Allah is to be rejected. From Ali it is related that he ruled concerning a man who married a woman and stipulated to her family that if he were to take another wife over her she would be divorced, or if he were to take a concubine over her the concubine would be free. He said: The condition of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, comes before their conditions. If he wishes, he fulfills his promise; and if he wishes, he marries another over her or takes a concubine, and no wife is divorced from him should he marry her, nor is any concubine freed should he take her. From Abu Jafar and Abu Abdullah the like of this is related.

It was narrated from Abu Jafar and Abu Abd-Allah (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), as likewise from Ali, that he gave judgment concerning a man who married a woman and stipulated that she should hold authority over her own affairs. Ali said: This departs from the Sunnah and assigns a right to one who is not its rightful holder. The husband is the guardian; intimacy and divorce rest in his hand. He therefore ruled that the dowry was owed by the husband, that intimacy and divorce remained his, and he nullified the condition.

Jafar ibn Muhammad said: A condition that is lawful, one that does not contradict the Book of Allah, is binding upon the man who married the woman on its basis. Among such valid conditions is that she shall remain with her family in a known land, or in a specified dwelling. This is permissible.

It was also narrated from him that he said: Whoever marries a woman on the condition that he will provide her a fixed daily maintenance and not be absent from her during the day, that condition does not invalidate the marriage, but neither is it itself binding; she retains the right to the division of nights and to the maintenance due to wives generally. Yet if a man marries a woman who fears that he may harm her or divorce her, and he agrees with her to forgo some of his rights regarding her maintenance and the division of nights, that is permissible, in accordance with the words of Allah the Almighty: "If a woman fears discord or desertion from her husband, there is no blame upon them if they come to an agreement between themselves" (al-Nisa 128).

Abu Abd-Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad said: If he stipulates for her that, should he take another wife or take a concubine, she shall have one hundred dinars or whatever sum he has bound himself to, the marriage is permissible. If the sum he has committed is drawn from the original dowry, it is binding; if it rests only upon the added stipulation, it is not binding. This is the meaning of the saying of Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali: A man should not make the divorce of one wife a condition for marrying another. The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) forbade a woman to seek the divorce of her sister wife so that she might take her place, for Allah the Almighty is the One who provides for her. And the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) forbade the marriage of pleasure (mutah).

Concerning the marriage of pleasure which some had allowed: it is reported that a man would say to a woman, "Give yourself to me in marriage," and would say, "I marry you for this dirham," or two dirhams, or whatever sum was named, for a single union, or a day, or two days, or whatever term they agreed upon. They said that once they agreed on this it became permissible for him until the end of the agreed term; and when the term expired the separation occurred of itself, without divorce. They claimed there was no iddah upon her, that she did not inherit from him nor he from her, and that intimacy by this arrangement was not permissible with a virgin, though some of them claimed it was permissible even with women already married. This is pure fornication, in which there is no ambiguity and which admits of no covering. Allah the Almighty has permitted intimacy only through two paths, through the bond of marriage and through the right hand of possession (milk al-yamin), for the Almighty said: "Those who guard their private parts, except with their wives or what their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy; but whoever seeks beyond that, those are the transgressors" (al-Muminun 5–7).

> يَٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِىُّ إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ وَأَحْصُوا۟ ٱلْعِدَّةَ

For if this pleasure union were a marriage, the woman could not be parted from the man without divorce and without iddah, since Allah the Almighty says: "O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period" (al-Talaq 1); and she would inherit and be inherited from, since Allah says: "And you shall have half of what your wives leave" (al-Nisa 12), and "They shall have a fourth of what you leave" (al-Nisa 12); and the child would be attached to them both, for the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) said: "The child belongs to the bed," meaning to the owner of the bed. But in this arrangement there is neither marriage nor right of possession, and what remains is forbidden. The reports forbidding the marriage of pleasure from the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) are many, as is his saying, "There is no marriage except with a guardian and two upright witnesses." Those who uphold the marriage of pleasure themselves claim that it is contracted without a guardian and without witnesses, and so it cannot stand. It was narrated from Ali, Abu Jafar, and Abu Abd-Allah that they declared the marriage of pleasure void, forbade it, and prohibited it.

It was narrated from Ali that he gave judgment concerning a slave-woman who had fled from her master and deceived a man by claiming to be free, so that he married her on that basis and she bore him children; then her master established his claim over her. He ruled that she be returned to her master, and that the man who had been deceived owed her master the value of his children by her, unless the master chose to grant the children to their father. If the man had bought her and she bore him a child, and her master then established his claim, she was to be returned to the one whose right was vindicated, and the value of the child was owed by the father, who could in turn recover it from the one who had sold her to him. But if he had taken her by force, or had known when he married her that she was owned and that her master had not given her in marriage, then both she and her child belonged to the master.

From Ali it was narrated concerning a free woman whom a male slave had approached, claiming to be free, so that she married him on that basis and then learned that he was owned: they may be separated if the woman wishes. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali said: She holds authority over her own decision; if she wishes she may remain with him, and if she wishes she may leave him. If she chooses to separate and the marriage has not been consummated, she is owed nothing; but if it has been consummated, she is entitled to her dowry, and the liability falls upon whoever deceived her, whether the slave himself or another. When the slave is freed, if his lord does not give him in marriage to her, the dowry rests with the slave once he is free; and if the lord gave him in marriage, or gave him leave to marry her, then her dowry is owed by the lord.

It was narrated from Ali, Abu Jafar, and Abu Abd-Allah concerning a man to whom another woman was brought as a bride, so that he consummated the marriage believing her to be his wife and only afterward learned otherwise: he must return that woman, and she is entitled to a dowry for what was done to her, claimed against the one who deceived him, and his true wife, the one he had actually married, is to be restored to him.

It was narrated from them concerning a man who is impotent and unable to approach women, yet conceals this from the woman he marries: she has the right of choice once she comes to know, and she is entitled to the dowry if she exercises that choice and the marriage has been consummated. They also said concerning a man who marries a woman and finds in her leprosy, or vitiligo, or blindness, or insanity, or a condition in the private parts that prevents intercourse, or a manifest lameness: the husband has the right of choice; if he wishes he may keep her, and if he wishes he may return her. She is entitled to the dowry if he has had intercourse with her, and his claim for it is against the one who deceived him with her, while the woman herself owes nothing in return. For defects other than these she is not to be returned.

It was narrated from Ali concerning a man who marries a woman as a virgin and finds her otherwise: he saw nothing objectionable in this, and said that virginity may be lost through a leap, through ablution, or through the passing of long years.

Mentioning the Forbidden Marriage and the Permissible Marriage

Allah the Almighty said: "And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women, except what has already passed; it is an indecency and a hateful thing and an evil way. Forbidden to you are your mothers, your daughters..." (al-Nisa 22–23). Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has thus forbidden in the plain text of His Book the marriage of those He named explicitly, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Imams of his house made clear what required clarification.

> وَرَبَٓئِبُكُمُ ٱلَّتِى فِى حُجُورِكُم مِّن نِّسَآئِكُمُ ٱلَّتِى دَخَلْتُم بِهِنَّ فَإِن لَّمْ تَكُونُوا۟ دَخَلْتُم بِهِنَّ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ

It came from Ali and Abu Abd-Allah concerning the mention of the mothers of wives that the matter is unrestricted: when a man marries a woman, her mother becomes forbidden to him, whether or not he has consummated the marriage with the daughter. They said: if a man marries a woman and then divorces her, or she dies before he has consummated the marriage, the marriage of her daughter remains lawful for him, in keeping with the words of Allah: "And your stepdaughters under your guardianship, born of your wives with whom you have consummated marriage; but if you have not consummated with them, there is no blame upon you" (al-Nisa 23). The "guardianship" here is the bond of inviolability. But if he has consummated the marriage with the woman, her daughter becomes forbidden to him; and likewise, if he has seen of her what is forbidden to other men, he may not marry her daughter.

It was narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad concerning a man who marries a woman and then dies leaving her, or divorces her before consummation: she is forbidden to his son for all the generations that descend, and to his fathers however far they ascend. And if a man looks upon his bondswoman with desire, or touches her, or looks upon her nakedness, she becomes forbidden to his sons and to his fathers. But if one of them owned her and did not approach her, nor touch her, nor look upon her with desire, and then the other came to own her, she is lawful to him. They permitted the owning of two sisters together, while forbidding their combination in marriage. They said: if a man has approached one of the two, the other becomes forbidden to him, and he may not approach the second until the first has left his ownership through manumission, sale, or gift; and it does not suffice for him to give her to his son. If she dies, the other becomes lawful to him; what is forbidden is only their combination in marriage, for Allah says: "And that you combine two sisters" (al-Nisa 23), making no exception there between the owned woman and the free.

It was narrated from Ali, Abu Jafar, and Abu Abd-Allah that a man should not marry the sister of a woman he has divorced until her iddah has elapsed and his right of revocation over her is extinguished; for so long as that right remains, he has effectively joined the two sisters together. But if the divorce was a final and irrevocable one, he may marry her sister, or another, provided he has no more than three other free wives besides her. They also said that a woman may not be joined with her paternal aunt, nor with her maternal aunt. Ali said: The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) forbade that, and made it unlawful. The daughter of Hamza was offered to him in marriage, and he said: Do you not know that she is the daughter of my brother through suckling, for I was nursed together with Hamza.

They saw no harm in joining the daughters of paternal uncles with the daughters of maternal uncles, nor in a man's marrying both his wife and a daughter of his by another. Likewise, when a man divorces a woman or dies and another man marries her thereafter, there is no harm in the son of her first husband, by another wife, marrying the daughter of her second husband by another wife. They said: if a man commits fornication with the mother of his wife, or her sister, or her daughter, this does not corrupt his marriage, for the unlawful does not corrupt the lawful. But if he commits fornication with a woman and she then bears a child, it is not proper for his son by another wife to marry that woman's daughter. They granted permission regarding the woman with whom a man had committed fornication once both have repented.

It was narrated from Ali concerning a woman who commits adultery before her husband has consummated the marriage with her: they are separated, she is owed no dowry, and the prescribed punishment (hadd) is carried out upon her. Her dowry is forfeited because the offense arose from her side. Yet the separation rests upon the husband's wish: if he holds to her, she remains his wife.

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, when asked about a sick man who contracts a marriage and then dies, said: the marriage is valid, and she inherits from him.

It was narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad concerning a man who marries two sisters, or five women, in a single marriage contract: the one whose name was mentioned first among the sisters at the time of the contract has a valid marriage, and four of the five women have valid marriages, while the marriage of the second sister, and of the fifth woman after the four, is annulled. If it cannot be known which was named first, the whole contract is void. They said concerning a man who marries a woman during her iddah, or marries her while one of the two is in a state of consecration, both knowing that this is not lawful: they are separated, and she is never again lawful to him. But if they were ignorant, they are separated, and they may contract anew once she becomes lawful to suitors.

Mentioning the Missing Husband

We have narrated from Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali that he said: if a man is reported dead to his family, so that his wife observes her iddah and then remarries, and afterward the first husband returns, the first husband has the greater right to her, whether or not the second husband has consummated the marriage. If the second husband has consummated it, she is entitled to her dowry for what was made lawful from her.

Jafar ibn Muhammad said: the wife of the missing man is to be left in her state so long as she keeps silent. But if she brings her case before the governor, he sets for her a term of four years and writes to inquire after her husband. If four years pass and no news of him comes, the governor summons the guardian of the missing man and asks whether the missing man has wealth. If he has wealth from which she may be maintained, and the guardian spends upon her from it, or the guardian spends upon her from his own means, then she has no way to remarry. But if the guardian will not maintain her and the missing man has no wealth, the governor compels the guardian to divorce her with a single pronouncement at the onset of her iddah while she is in a state of purity, and the guardian's divorce stands as the husband's divorce. If her husband returns before her iddah is complete, he has the greater right to her; and if her iddah has ended, she is lawful to suitors.

It was said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family), what is to be done if the guardian provides for her and she says, "I cannot be patient; I want what other women have"? He answered that she has no such recourse, and no claim to it, so long as the guardian provides for her.

The missing man (al-mafqud) is one who has departed his home and whose whereabouts are unknown. He may have been seen between the two battle lines in time of war, after which the people scattered and he was lost; or he may have set sail on a ship that capsized; or it may simply be that no one on the journey knows where he settled. As for a man whose location is known, his ruling is not that of the missing man. The ruling concerning his wife is that of a woman whose husband is merely absent (ghaib): she may not remarry unless he dies or divorces her. He said: if the whereabouts of the absent man are known, his wife may not remarry.

On Breastfeeding (al-Rida)

> وَرَبَٓئِبُكُمُ ٱلَّتِى فِى حُجُورِكُم مِّن نِّسَآئِكُمُ ٱلَّتِى دَخَلْتُم بِهِنَّ فَإِن لَّمْ تَكُونُوا۟ دَخَلْتُم بِهِنَّ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ

I have mentioned above the saying of Allah Almighty: ﴿وَأُمَّهَاتُكُمُ اللَّاتِي أَرْضَعْنَكُمْ وَأَخَوَاتُكُم مِّنَ الرَّضَاعَةِ﴾, "and your mothers who have suckled you, and your sisters through breastfeeding." We have narrated from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah ((ع), and) that what is forbidden through lineage is forbidden through breastfeeding. I have already set out which of the women are forbidden in marriage, and whoever comes, through breastfeeding, to occupy the place of one of these holds the same status of prohibition.

It is permissible for a man to marry a woman who has breastfed his sons, and to marry from among her daughters those she did not nurse him alongside, because she is not his mother through breastfeeding and is not a wife to his father. He may likewise marry her daughter when the woman is among the daughters of a woman who breastfed his brother or his sister. In the same way, a man may marry the daughters of women who breastfed his son, and their daughters, for they did not nurse his son, and there is no bond between them and him, whether through breastfeeding or otherwise. What is forbidden is to marry the nursing woman herself; but the daughters of paternal uncles and aunts, and of maternal uncles and aunts, through breastfeeding are lawful to marry, just as they are lawful through lineage. A man may marry a woman while his father marries her daughter by another man, and a father and son may each marry one of two sisters.

It was narrated from Ali that he said: breastfeeding makes forbidden whether it be little or much; even a single suckle creates prohibition, by the saying of Allah Almighty, ﴿وَأُمَّهَاتُكُمُ اللَّاتِي أَرْضَعْنَكُمْ﴾, "and your mothers who have suckled you." Breastfeeding applies to the little and the much alike, for even a small quantity nourishes, and from it flesh and blood grow and bone is strengthened in proportion.

It was narrated from Ali that he said: the breastfeeding that creates prohibition is that which occurs within the two years, for Allah says: ﴿وَالْوَالِدَاتُ يُرْضِعْنَ أَوْلَادَهُنَّ حَوْلَيْنِ كَامِلَيْنِ لِمَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يُتِمَّ الرَّضَاعَةَ﴾, "and mothers shall suckle their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the suckling." What occurs after the two years is not breastfeeding and creates no prohibition. The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) said: "لَا رِضَاعَ بَعْدَ فِطَامٍ," "There is no breastfeeding after weaning."

It is narrated from Ali, Abu Jafar, and Abu Abd Allah concerning a woman who gives her husband her milk to drink in order, by that pretense, to make herself forbidden to him, or who gives it to her bondswoman, or nurses her, to make her forbidden to him: they said that the man should discipline his wife, but that this creates no prohibition for him, because the breastfeeding of an adult is not breastfeeding. If a man is suckled after two years have passed from his birth, or a wife gives her husband her milk to drink, nothing is thereby made forbidden. But whatever occurs before the two years, whether by suckling, or by drinking a woman's milk, or by its being administered into the throat (wajur) or the nose (saut), is breastfeeding.

They said: the milk of the stallion creates prohibition, meaning the milk attributed to the man who fathered it. This is when a man has several wives, or umm-walad mothers, in his household, and one of them nurses a slave boy while another nurses a slave girl: the two become siblings through breastfeeding, even though they did not nurse at the breast of one woman, because the one father unites them and they were nursed by the milk of his wives, so the milk is attributed to him.

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali was asked about the wife of a man who nursed a slave girl: is it lawful for his son by another woman to marry her? He said: No. It was said to him: does she then stand to him as a sister through breastfeeding? He said: Yes, from the father's side. He said: a man had two wives, each of whom bore a son, and one of the two wives nursed a slave girl belonging to other people. He said: the other son may not marry this slave girl, for she was nursed by the milk of the same father, and what lineage forbids, breastfeeding forbids.

He was asked about a slave girl belonging to a man, whom his wife, or the mother of his child, claimed to have nursed. He said: she is not to be believed, for she is drawing something to herself. Concerning a woman who said she had nursed a slave boy and a slave girl and then denied it, he said: if she denies it, that stands. It was said to him: and if she afterward retracts her denial and claims again that she nursed them? He said: she is not to be believed. The testimony of a single upright woman is accepted in matters of breastfeeding; but if no upright woman is available, her testimony alone does not suffice.

They forbade seeking a wet-nurse whose milk comes of fornication, as with a woman who commits adultery and bears a child by it: such a woman should not be sought as a wet-nurse, nor taken as a foster-nurse (zir), neither she nor her daughter born of adultery. Yet they permitted seeking a wet-nurse among polytheist women if they are within a marriage, while disliking the seeking of a wet-nurse from the milk of those known for enmity toward the family of Muhammad ((ع) and his family). Breastfeeding by the milk of fornication makes nothing forbidden. Jafar ibn Muhammad said: unlawful milk does not render the lawful unlawful, as with a woman nursed first by lawful milk and afterward by the milk of fornication. He said: whoever nurses a girl with the milk of fornication does not thereby make it forbidden to marry her, because unlawful milk does not render the lawful forbidden.

It was narrated from Ali that he ruled concerning a man who married a woman, gave her her dowry, and had not yet consummated the marriage, after which it was established that there was a nursing relationship between them: she must return to him what she had taken. And it was narrated from the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) that he forbade women to nurse freely those boys whom they do not know.

On the Marriage of Bondswomen (Nikah al-Ima)

> وَمَن لَّمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنكُمْ طَوْلًا أَن يَنكِحَ ٱلْمُحْصَنَتِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنَتِ فَمِن مَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَنُكُم مِّن فَتَيَتِكُمُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنَتِ

Allah Almighty said: ﴿وَمَن لَّمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنكُمْ طَوْلًا أَن يَنكِحَ الْمُحْصَنَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ فَمِن مَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُم مِّن فَتَيَاتِكُمُ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾, up to His saying ﴿ذَٰلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ الْعَنَتَ مِنكُمْ ۚ وَأَن تَصْبِرُوا خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾: "And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women, then from those whom your right hands possess, of your believing bondswomen," up to His saying, "That is for him among you who fears falling into sin; and that you be patient is better for you, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful."

It was narrated from Ali, commenting on the words of Allah Almighty ﴿ذَٰلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ الْعَنَتَ مِنكُمْ﴾, "That is for him among you who fears falling into sin," that he said: this means adultery, nothing else. So a free Muslim should not marry a bondswoman until he fears being overcome by desire and cannot find the means to marry a free woman. If he has the means to a free woman, he should not marry a bondswoman; and if he does not fear falling into sin, he likewise should not marry her, for Allah Almighty has permitted free men the marriage of bondswomen only upon these two conditions.

Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad said: a free man may not marry a bondswoman until two conditions are joined in him, the fear of sin and the lack of means. If he is driven to it, let him marry her. When a free man marries a bondswoman, the children she bears him belong to her master as slaves, unless he stipulates at the marriage that whatever children she bears him shall be free; if he stipulates that, they are free, and the ruling on the child follows the ruling on the mother, in freedom and in bondage. If a slave marries a free woman, their children are free, and his master may not stipulate that the free woman's children be slaves, as he might with the children of a bondswoman, because the freeing of a bondswoman's children rests with their master, who frees them if he wishes. A woman may not take ownership of her own children while they are free, nor may anyone else.

A bondswoman may not be given in marriage except with the permission of her master, for Allah says: ﴿فَانكِحُوهُنَّ بِإِذْنِ أَهْلِهِنَّ﴾, "So marry them with the permission of their families." If a bondswoman is jointly owned by two men, she is not lawful to either of them, even if the other permits it, because the part of a person cannot be divided, nor made lawful by gift. If one of the two gives her in marriage without the permission of his partner, the marriage is not valid unless the other ratifies it, and the husband may not consummate it until the second owner permits the marriage; if he does not permit it, the marriage is dissolved. Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked about a bondswoman jointly owned by two men, one of whom gives her in marriage while the other is absent: is the marriage valid? He said: if the absent owner is averse to it, it is not valid.

It was narrated from Ali that he said: it is not lawful for a free Muslim to marry a Jewish or a Christian bondswoman, for Allah Almighty says ﴿مِّن فَتَيَاتِكُمُ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾, "of your believing bondswomen." Likewise a free man should not marry a Magian or a polytheist bondswoman; for were that lawful, the polytheists would come to enslave the children of the Muslims. If a man wishes to marry a bondswoman, let him free her first, and then marry her if he wishes and she wishes. The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) married Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab and drew the veil (حِجَاب) over her. Jafar ibn Muhammad said: any man who frees his slave woman and wishes to marry her, let it be with witnesses and an appointed dower; and if he makes her emancipation her dower, that is permitted, as I have explained in the foregoing.

A woman under a contract of emancipation (mukatabah) may be married with the permission of her master. Ali was asked about the marriage of a mukatabah, and he said: she may marry; and whatever child is born to her during her contract of emancipation stands in her own position, so that of that child what is freed in her is freed, and what remains in bondage in her remains in bondage. We shall mention in the chapter on those under emancipation contracts how this is reckoned, if Allah wills.

It was narrated from Ali that he said concerning a man who marries a bondswoman over a free wife: they are to be separated, and he is charged her dower for what he made lawful of her person if he consummated the marriage; if he did not consummate it, she is owed nothing. Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad said: if a man marries a free woman alongside a bondswoman and the free woman knows of it, he may divide his time, two portions to the free woman and one portion to the bondswoman. If the free woman did not know that he had a bondswoman when he married her, and afterward learns of it, she has the choice: if she wishes she may remain, and if she wishes she may leave his bond, and she is owed the dower for what he made lawful of her person if he consummated the marriage; but if he did not consummate it and she chooses to part from him, she is owed nothing.

It was narrated from him that he said: it is not lawful for a free man to marry a bondswoman by herself. If he marries a free woman and a bondswoman in a single contract, one looks to whose name began the contract: if the free woman's name began it, the marriage of the bondswoman is void; but if the bondswoman's name began it and the free woman accepts to remain alongside her, the marriage of both is established, provided the man is one for whom the marriage of bondswomen is lawful, as we have described. A man may contract marriage upon a free woman while lacking the means for her dower; but if he does have the means, the marriage of the bondswoman is void, whether he began with her or named her second. Likewise, if it is not known with which of them the marriage of the bondswoman began, the marriage of the bondswoman is invalid.

He was asked about the maintenance (نَفَقَة) of a bondswoman wife. He said: when a free man marries a bondswoman, she serves her people by day and comes to her husband by night, and he owes her maintenance when they do this; but if they bar her from him by night, he owes her no maintenance.

Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked about a man who has young children who own a slave girl: may he lie with her? He said: if he desires her, let him set a just value upon himself for her, so that her price stands against him as a debt to his children; then he owns her and may lie with her if he wishes. But if the children are grown, she is not lawful to him unless they sell her to him, and it is not lawful for him to do otherwise. A man has no right to any part of his child's wealth except by the child's own goodwill, save that, if he is driven to it, he may eat of it what sustains him, in the customary measure and without indulgence, when he is in hardship and the child is wealthy.

It was narrated from him that he was asked about a man who had a slave girl, and his wife, fearing he would take her for himself, ordered her son to lie with her, and he did. He said: she has sinned, and her son has sinned, and the son is liable to the prescribed punishment (hadd) if he is an adult. And he disliked that men should approach her, even though she is thereby forbidden to the master, because the unlawful does not render the lawful forbidden.

It was narrated from Ali that he disliked a man's lying with a bondswoman over whom another holds a stipulated right. The mudabbarah may be married with the permission of her master, and her ruling remains that of a bondswoman until her master dies, whereupon she is freed. If a bondswoman is freed while she has a husband: if her husband is free, she remains his wife and has no choice; but if he is a slave, she has the choice, upon being freed, to remain with him or to leave.

The matter of the freed slave woman is settled by what the Messenger of Allah and his family, did with Barirah. She was a slave woman married to a slave man, and she was grieved by her situation. When she was set free, the Messenger of Allah gave her the choice, and she chose herself rather than her husband. He then ordered her to observe a waiting period of three menstrual cycles. And he said: if her master assists her to fulfill her emancipation contract, even if she is elderly, she has no right of choice against her husband on account of that assistance.

**The marriage of slaves**

Allah, exalted be the One who speaks, said: ﴿ عَبْدًا مَمْلُوكًا لَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَىٰ شَيْءٍ ﴾, "A slave who is owned and has no power over anything" (al-Nahl: 75). The Messenger of Allah and his family, forbade a slave to marry without the permission of his master. He said: any free woman who gives herself in marriage to a slave without the permission of her guardian has made her person unlawful and is owed no dower, meaning if the master denies the marriage. But if the master permits his slave to marry, then it is valid, and the dower falls upon the master when he is content with it.

Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked about a man who marries his own slave woman to one of his male slaves. He said: he says, "I have given her to you in marriage," and he gives her some small thing as a dower. The right of separation remains in the hand of the master: if he wishes he may part them without a divorce, and if he sells the slave man, that selling is itself a separation between them; and if he sells them together, the buyer may part them if he wishes.

Jafar ibn Muhammad said: if a slave woman is sold and she has a free husband, she remains his wife, and her person is not lawful to the buyer until her husband divorces her or dies and she completes her waiting period. From Ali: if a woman comes to own her husband, or any portion of him, the marriage between them is dissolved by the ownership itself, and she becomes the owner of her own person. It is not lawful for a woman to marry her own slave unless she first frees him; if she wishes, she may free him and then marry him afterward.

From Jafar ibn Muhammad: the slave may purchase and may approach of the slave women whatever his master has permitted him, and he may not marry more than two free women. He may marry four slave women, and the divorce of those he marries rests in the hand of his master, who may divorce them on his behalf whenever he wishes.

**The marriage of polytheists**

The marriages of polytheists among themselves, whether they belong to a single religious community or to differing ones, are valid when contracted according to what their own religion requires, and it is not fitting that such marriages be annulled. We have narrated from Ali that he said: if a man and his wife are taken among the spoils, their marriage holds, and even if her husband is captured some days after her, they remain as they were, unless one of them is carried off and brought into the House of Islam. If that occurs, their marriage is dissolved, and she is not lawful to him except by a new contract, even if one of them had been taken before the other. So long as either of them remains a captive among the spoils, for as long as they remain there, their marriage stands between them. But once one of them enters the House of Islam, their marriage is dissolved. If she embraces Islam and her husband is then captured after her acceptance of Islam, and she has passed three menstrual cycles, yet she had not been carried off and her husband had not embraced Islam, then they remain upon their marriage. The one who owns them both may separate them if he wishes, as he may do with the rest of his slaves, unless at the time of their capture they were granted safe conduct on the condition that they not be parted, and that was contracted for them, in which case their separation is not obligatory.

From Ali: it is not lawful for Muslims to marry polytheist women in the abode of war while the rulings of the polytheists hold sway over them. And from him: if a woman of the people of war seeks safe conduct and comes out to the House of Islam while she has a polytheist husband, his marital bond to her is severed, and she may marry if she wishes after her womb has been cleared. Should her husband then come as a Muslim under safe conduct, he has no claim upon her except by a renewed marriage, because when she came out to the House of Islam his bond to her was already severed.

If a man embraces Islam while he has a polytheist wife, she remains his wife. But if a woman embraces Islam while her husband remains a polytheist, a separation is made between them. If her husband embraces Islam before her waiting period has ended, they remain upon their marriage; if her waiting period has expired, she becomes the owner of her own person.

From Ali and Abu Jafar both: they forbade marriage with the Christian women of the Arabs and the eating of their slaughtered animals. From Ali: an apostate who renounces his faith and joins the abode of war is in the standing of a dead man. His wealth is divided among his heirs, his wives observe the waiting period of widows, and they may then marry if they wish.

From Jafar ibn Muhammad: if a woman embraces Islam while her husband remains a polytheist, she is separated from him should he not embrace Islam, and she keeps her full dower; if he had not consummated the marriage with her, she is entitled to half the dower. And if polytheists embrace Islam, they remain upon their existing marriages. The Messenger of Allah and his family, said: "Confirm the people of the age of ignorance upon whatever state they entered Islam, whether of marriage, divorce, or inheritance."

From Ali concerning the polytheist who embraces Islam while he has two free sisters as wives, or more than four free wives: he is left with the first of the two sisters he married, and a separation is made between him and the second, and between him and whatever wives he took beyond the four free women. And from him: Allah made the women of the People of the Book lawful for the Muslims only when Muslim women were few; and when Muslim women became many, Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿ وَلَا تَنْكِحُوا الْمُشْرِكَاتِ حَتَّى يُؤْمِنَّ ﴾, "And do not marry polytheist women until they believe" (al-Baqarah: 221). And He said: ﴿ وَلَا تُمْسِكُوا بِعِصَمِ الْكَوَافِرِ ﴾, "And do not hold to the marriage bonds of disbelieving women" (al-Mumtahanah: 10). The Messenger of Allah and his family, forbade a Muslim man to marry a non-Muslim woman while he is able to find a Muslim woman, and forbade a polytheist to marry a Muslim woman.

If a polytheist embraces Islam while he has a polytheist wife, he may keep her with him if he desires her, in the hope that Allah, mighty and majestic, will guide her, and he may marry above her up to three Muslim women, if she is aware of her standing. If he marries a Muslim woman while he still has a polytheist wife, and the Muslim woman does not know of this, and she learns of it after consummation, then the matter is placed in her own hand: if she wishes to remain with him she may stay, and if she wishes to depart she may go. She is entitled to her dower for what was made lawful of her person, and she may marry whomever she wishes once her waiting period has elapsed, without need of a divorce. But if he divorces the polytheist wife before the waiting period has elapsed, counted from the day the Muslim wife made her choice, then he has the greater right to her.

**The division of turns among co-wives**

Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿ وَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا بَيْنَ النِّسَاءِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ فَلَا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ فَتَذَرُوهَا كَالْمُعَلَّقَةِ ﴾, "You will never be able to deal justly between wives, even though you are eager to do so; yet do not incline altogether away, so as to leave her as one suspended" (al-Nisa: 129). Thus the Exalted in praise made known that justice between wives in matters of affection, desire, and ardor, apart from intercourse, cannot be attained, while in matters of maintenance, lodging, gifts, and the like, justice can indeed be practiced. So it is upon a man, if he has several wives, to be with each of them by day and night in turn.

Jafar ibn Muhammad was asked about a man who has wives and is intimate with some of them and not others. He said: it is upon him to spend with each one her night, and to remain with her through her morning. If he is not stirred to intercourse, nothing is held against him; but if a man is stirred to intercourse while he is with one of his wives, it is not fitting that he abandon this and withhold himself for another.

From Ali when he was asked about a man who has wives and then sets out on a journey: he said, when he returns let him begin with the one whose right of a turn is due. And from him: if a man has only one wife, it is not fitting that he leave her without spending the night with her one night out of four, and in the remaining three he may do what Allah has made lawful for him.

Jafar ibn Muhammad said: if a man has two wives, he may set apart one of them for the three nights that are his own and assign to the other her single night. Likewise, if he has three wives, he assigns to each her night and devotes the fourth to whichever of them he wishes. If he has four, he may not favor one of them above another.

From Ali concerning a man who has a wife or several wives and then marries again: if he marries a virgin, he stays with her seven nights, and if he marries a woman previously married, he stays with her three nights; thereafter he divides the nights equally among his wives. He was asked about the words of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿ وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزًا أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا أَنْ يُصْلِحَا بَيْنَهُمَا صُلْحًا وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ ﴾, "If a woman fears ill treatment or aversion from her husband, there is no blame upon them if they reach a reconciliation between themselves, and reconciliation is best" (al-Nisa: 128). He said: this concerns a man who has two wives and becomes unable to fulfill the rights of one of them, or she is a dhimmi woman, so he inclines toward the other and wishes to divorce the first, while she dislikes that. So she reconciles with him on the condition that he come to her from time to time, or that she yield to him her share of that.

**Maintenance owed to wives**

> قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا فَرَضْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ فِىٓ أَزْوَجِهِمْ وَمَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَنُهُمْ

Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿ قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا فَرَضْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ فِي أَزْوَاجِهِمْ وَمَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ ﴾, "We have known what We have made obligatory upon them concerning their wives and those whom their right hands possess" (al-Ahzab: 50). And the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿ وَارْزُقُوهُمْ فِيهَا وَاكْسُوهُمْ وَقُولُوا لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفًا ﴾, "And provide for them therein and clothe them, and speak to them words of kindness" (al-Nisa: 5).

It is narrated from the family of the Messenger of Allah that he addressed the people in the Farewell Pilgrimage, mentioned the women, and enjoined the people to treat them well, saying: "They have over you their sustenance and their clothing in a fitting manner." He forbade and his family, that a man eat his fill while his family goes hungry, and said: "It is enough sin for a man that he neglect those whom he supports." It is narrated from him and his family, that he said: "There are seven among the foremost of deeds, so keep to them," and he mentioned among them maintenance for one's dependents. And from him and his family: "The severest of trials is many dependents with little wealth, and few dependents is one of the two forms of ease." And from him and his family: "Whoever is moderate in his livelihood, Allah provides for him, and whoever is wasteful, Allah deprives him." And from him and his family: "When Allah, mighty and majestic, intends good for a household, He grants them understanding in religion, provides them gentleness in their livelihood, and grants them moderation in their affairs." And from him and his family: "Gentle moderation is half of livelihood; no man who lives in moderation is ever in want."

From Ali: if a man finds nothing to spend upon his wife, he is given a respite; if he brings her something, meaning what suffices to feed her, they are not separated, and if he finds nothing at all he is granted a term, and then they are separated. And from him: a woman complained against her husband that he would not maintain her, intending harm to her, so he imprisoned him on account of her maintenance. And he said: any woman who leaves her husband's house without his permission is owed no maintenance until she returns.

And from him concerning the man who divorces his wife while she is nursing his child by her: she has the better right to the nursing, and she takes from him what would be given to a wet nurse. And if her husband dies and leaves with her a child of his whom she nurses, she is entitled to the like of a nurse's wage drawn from the child's wealth, if the child has wealth from inheritance or otherwise, and the guardian has no right to remove the child from her lap.

> وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَنفَقُوا۟ لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا۟ وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا۟ وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ قَوَامًۭا

Maintenance owed to wives, and to those relatives upon whom it is obligatory, is according to one's means and capacity. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿ لِيُنْفِقْ ذُو سَعَةٍ مِنْ سَعَتِهِ وَمَنْ قُدِرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقُهُ فَلْيُنْفِقْ مِمَّا آتَاهُ اللَّهُ ﴾, "Let a man of ample means spend out of his ampleness, and whoever has his provision straitened, let him spend out of what Allah has given him" (al-Talaq: 7). So the ruler imposes upon the one obliged the maintenance of his like, without extravagance and without stinting. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿ وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا أَنْفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ قَوَامًا ﴾, "And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stinting, but hold a just balance between the two" (al-Furqan: 67).

> لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا

This is a thing well known and not obscure, requiring no recourse to opinion or independent reasoning, for its measure is known to people from their customary provisions in every place and time, and according to want and plenty, the means at hand, cheapness and dearness, poverty and wealth. Every poor person who is unable to manage or to work, his maintenance falls upon the one who would inherit from him were he to die, in proportion to what that heir would receive of his estate, except the wife, for her maintenance is upon her husband and he owes her no return. If the one upon whom the maintenance is obligatory is himself poor and has nothing to spend, then his case is like that of one who has no guardian to provide for him: he seeks his provision from the provision of Allah, glorified be His mention. A man is not bound to provide for one distant from him who would not inherit from him were he to die, when his own heir is poor and without wealth, because his maintenance is owed only there, and Allah, mighty and majestic, has excused him, for His words: ﴿ لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا ﴾, "Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity" (al-Baqarah: 286), and His words: ﴿ لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا مَا آتَاهَا ﴾, "Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it" (al-Talaq: 7). If he should afterward come into ease, he spends upon the one in his charge from that time onward, and he has no right to be held to account for what has already passed.

**Al-istibra, the clearing of the womb**

We have narrated from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah that a man of the Ansar invited the Messenger of Allah and his family, to a meal, and he accepted. At the Ansari's house there was a slave woman, great with child, going to and fro serving the food. The Messenger of Allah said to him: "What is this?" He said: "A slave woman of mine, whom I bought some days ago, and she is pregnant." He said: "Perhaps you have approached her?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, I have done so." Then the Messenger of Allah said to him: "Were it not for the sanctity of your food, I would have invoked upon you a curse that would enter upon you in your grave. Free what is in her womb, for your seed has already nourished its hearing, its sight, its flesh, its blood, its hair, and its skin."

And Ali said: it is not lawful for a man to approach a woman pregnant by another until she delivers what is in her womb and becomes pure; and if he purchases a slave woman who is pregnant, he must not approach her until she gives birth and becomes pure. And from the Messenger of Allah and his family: a slave woman, when a man would approach her, is to be cleared by one menstrual cycle.

On istibra

Ali said: whoever buys a young slave girl who has not yet reached puberty and has shown no sign of it, and over whom there is no fear of pregnancy, may approach her if he wishes and is under no obligation to perform istibra upon her. He said: whoever buys a slave girl who has despaired of menstruation should set her apart for two months and then approach her if he wishes. This applies when it is doubted that she may still menstruate, even though her menses appear to have ceased. Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad, the prayers of Allah be upon him, said: whoever buys an old woman and knows with certainty that she does not menstruate, there being no doubt in her case, may approach her if he wishes and need not perform istibra.

He said: whoever buys a slave girl from a woman may approach her before performing istibra, and there is no harm in that; yet if he performs istibra as a safeguard for himself, that is better. Istibra is, however, an obligation upon the seller: if he has approached the slave woman and then wishes to sell her, he must not sell her until he has performed istibra upon her by one menstrual cycle, lest she be carrying his child and his offspring be sold along with her.

It was narrated from Ali, the prayers of Allah be upon him, that he said: if a man buys a slave woman who does not menstruate, or one who has reached puberty without having menstruated, he must perform istibra upon her for forty-five nights.

Ali, the prayers of Allah be upon him, was asked about a man who bought a slave girl who had reached the age of discernment but had not menstruated and was a virgin, whose seller had taken her back and then sold her. He said: her case is grave; he must perform istibra upon her for nine months, and then he may approach her after the nine months if no pregnancy has appeared, taking the cautious course.

It was related from him concerning a man who buys a slave girl while she is in a state of purity, and her seller informs him that he has not approached her since she last menstruated nor during the present purity in which she is. He said: if the seller is trustworthy in his eyes, he may approach her if he wishes; and if he performs istibra, that is the more cautious course for him. He said: whoever buys a slave girl who has had no husband, and whose master has not approached her, must nonetheless perform istibra upon her by one menstrual cycle.

He was asked about a man who bought a slave girl, then freed her and married her, whether he might approach her. He said: let him perform istibra of her womb by one menstrual cycle; and if he approaches her before performing istibra, there is no harm in it. It was narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad that he was asked about a man who had lain with a slave woman of his and then wished to give her in marriage before performing istibra. He said: No. It was said to him: by how much should he perform istibra? He said: by one menstrual cycle, though two are more beloved to me. A man must likewise perform istibra of the slave woman when he wishes to sell her, just as he performs it when he buys her.

It was narrated from Ali, the prayers of Allah be upon him, that he said: when a man buys a slave woman, there is no harm in his enjoying of her what is short of intercourse before he performs istibra, meaning fondling, kissing, and approach short of the private part. It was narrated from him that he was asked about a man who bought a slave woman and feared she might be pregnant; he said: let him perform istibra upon her for forty-five nights.

He was asked about a slave woman who had committed adultery, whether her master might approach her. He said: he does not approach her until he has performed istibra upon her. And if a man commits adultery with a slave woman and then buys her, he ought not to approach her until he has performed istibra upon her; and if she has conceived by him through that adultery, the child is not attributed to him, for the Messenger of Allah said: "الْوَلَدُ لِلْفِرَاشِ وَالْعَاهِرُ الْحَجَرُ," meaning the child belongs to the marriage bed, and for the fornicator is the stone.

It was narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad that he said: whoever buys a slave girl while she is menstruating, when she becomes pure let him approach her if he wishes. And it was narrated from Ali that he said concerning a woman taken captive who has a husband: she performs istibra by one menstrual cycle, and when she is pure her master may approach her. And if a woman is coerced and violated, her husband does not approach her until she has performed istibra by one menstrual cycle.

edits.chapter_key: freedom, generosity, and the division of estates
edits.body_md:
### Gifts, Bequests, and the Shares of Inheritance

### On Gifts and Generosity

Gifts, good works, and beneficence offered for the sake of God Almighty and in pursuit of His reward hold within them virtue, righteousness, and recompense. The Messenger of God, (ع) and his family, said: "All of creation are the children of God, and the most beloved of creation to God Almighty is the one who benefits His children, who brings joy to a household, and who walks with a Muslim brother in his time of need." Such a person, he said, is more beloved to God Almighty than two months of itikaf in the Sacred Mosque.

Ali, prayers of God be upon him, said that the people of goodness stand in greater need of having their goodness accepted than the needy stand in need of them, because through that goodness come praise, reward, and remembrance for them from God. Whoever performs a kind act toward one of God's creatures has in truth ennobled himself by it and adorned his own honor.

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, prayers of God be upon him, said: "When God raises the believer from his grave, there goes forth with him a beautiful figure. When he passes through those terrors, it says to him, Do not fear, no harm shall come to you, and it does not cease to reassure him and give him glad tidings until it brings him before God, who calls him to an easy reckoning and then commands that he be taken to Paradise. The believer says to it, Who are you, may God have mercy upon you? You promised me and were truthful to me and gave me security. It replies, I am a creation your Lord fashioned out of the joy you used to bring to the believers. Today it is I who gladden you."

Jafar ibn Muhammad, prayers of God be upon him, said: "There is nothing more excellent than beneficence except its reward, and beneficence is a gift from God Almighty to His believing servant. Not everyone who loves to do good to people is opened to it, nor is everyone who desires it able to do it, nor is everyone who is able to do it given leave to do it. So when God Almighty bestows His grace upon a servant, He gathers together for him the desire for beneficence, the ability for it, and the leave to perform it. There, happiness and honor are complete, both for the one who seeks the good and the one to whom it is directed."

He said, (ع): "Beneficence is not made complete except by three qualities: making little of it, making it easy, and hastening it. When you make little of it, you have made it great in the eyes of the one to whom you do it; when you make it easy, you have rendered it complete for him; and when you hasten it, you have made it a cause of joy for him. But if you do not do these things, you have spoiled it and rendered it thankless."

He said: "The best of Muslims is the one who joins, helps, and gives." And he said: "I heard my father say: the doing of good wards off the calamities of evil. Every kindness is a charity, and the people of goodness in this world are the people of goodness in the Hereafter. The first to enter Paradise are the people of goodness."

The Messenger of God and his family, said: "Whoever has a kindness done to him, let him repay it; if he is unable, let him praise the one who did it; and if he does not, then he has been ungrateful for the blessing."

We have narrated from the Imams of the People of the House of the Messenger of God, prayers of God be upon them, that they permitted a man to favor some of his children over others with his wealth and his gifts if he wished. A gift or a charity is valid whether or not it has been taken into the recipient's possession. Whoever gives a gift for the sake of God Almighty, or to a blood relative or a kinsman, has no right to take it back. But if he gives a gift or grant intending to be compensated for it, that is disliked, and he may take it back if he is not compensated. And whoever gives a gift, or gives a charity, to a blood relative or kinsman who then dies, so that it returns to him by inheritance, in that there is no harm.

The umra, the ruqba, and the sukna are among the things in which there is merit and reward. The umra is that a man grants another man a house, an estate, or anything he may benefit from for the duration of his life. The ruqba is of the same meaning, except that it carries the condition that whichever of the two dies first, the property returns to the original grantor or to his heirs. If a man grants something for his own lifetime, then it is his while he lives. If the condition is set upon the life of the grantor and he dies, it returns to his heirs. If it is conditioned upon the lifetime of the recipient, then it is the recipient's for his life, and if the grantor dies, his heirs may not take it from the recipient's hands; he may dwell in it and inhabit it until he dies. And if the grantor made it for the recipient and his heirs, then it belongs to him and to them after him, according to how the grantor settled it.

Presents are commended when they are for the sake of God Almighty and for His face. There is no good in any present given to curry favor in a falsehood, or to seek a like return, or to obtain the fulfillment of a need, or to secure attention from the one to whom it is given. The fulfilling of a believer's needs and care for him in what is right is an obligation upon his believing brother; so if he takes payment for that, it is unlawful gain. Likewise is whatever he takes for collusion in falsehood.

> إِن تُبْدُوا۟ ٱلصَّدَقَتِ فَنِعِمَّا هِىَ ۖ وَإِن تُخْفُوهَا وَتُؤْتُوهَا ٱلْفُقَرَآءَ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌۭ لَّكُمْ

As for what is an imposed obligation, such as zakat and the like, the merit is to give it openly and to announce it. As for voluntary charity, the merit is to keep it secret, though if it is announced there is no harm in that. God, exalted be He, has said: ﴿إِنْ تُبْدُوا الصَّدَقَاتِ فَنِعِمَّا هِيَ وَإِنْ تُخْفُوهَا وَتُؤْتُوهَا الْفُقَرَاءَ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾ — "If you disclose your charities, that is good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, that is better for you." (Al-Baqarah: 271)

So it is with all the acts of righteousness: the disclosure and mention of their obligatory portions is good, while the concealment and secrecy of their voluntary portions is more excellent. The obligatory prayer is more excellent in the mosques and in congregation, while the voluntary prayer is more excellent in seclusion. If a man were to say, "I have prayed the noon prayer," or the afternoon prayer, or whatever obligatory prayer he names, there is no harm in his saying so; and likewise if he says, "I have fasted the month of Ramadan." But if he says, "I have risen for the night prayer," or "I have fasted such-and-such" of the voluntary acts, then that saying of his is disliked, on account of the ostentation it admits. Upon this principle run all deeds.

Whoever owns something but has not yet taken it into his possession may still give it in charity or as a gift. Whoever gives a charity is not permitted to take it back. Whoever sets something aside as an endowment for his child, his freed clients, or particular people he names, and removes it from his own hand and delivers it to them, that is valid, and it stands according to whatever condition he stipulates and the terms upon which he restricts it. If they later fall into dispute over it and corruption among them is feared, they may sell it if they wish and divide its price in proportion to what was assigned to each, provided it was set aside for them by name. But if he set it aside for them and their descendants, or said, "When they die out, it becomes a charity," then it is a charity and they are not permitted to sell it. If he made its final destination a charity, then when those for whom it was set aside die out it passes to the poor and the needy. If he did not make its final destination a charity, and those for whom it was endowed die out, it returns to him if he is living, or to whoever is entitled to his inheritance if he has died. If he stipulated that any of the women for whom the endowment was made who marries forfeits her right in it, and then they are widowed and return to it, the condition holds. And if he said, "If I am in need, I have the better right to it," then the endowment is void; it is part of his estate for his heirs if he dies, and he may take it back whenever he wishes.

### On Bequests

> كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ إِن تَرَكَ خَيْرًا ٱلْوَصِيَّةُ

God, exalted be He, has said: ﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ إِنْ تَرَكَ خَيْرًا الْوَصِيَّةُ﴾ — "It is prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you and he leaves wealth behind, that he make a bequest." (Al-Baqarah: 180) And death is present for every living soul, for none knows when it will come to him. He also said: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا شَهَادَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ حِينَ الْوَصِيَّةِ﴾ — "O you who believe, let there be testimony among you when death approaches one of you, at the time of the bequest." (Al-Maidah: 106)

The Messenger of God and his family, said: "It does not befit a Muslim to pass two nights except that his will is written and kept at his head." And he said and his family: "Whoever does not make his bequest well at the time of death has fallen short in his manliness and his reason." They asked, "O Messenger of God, how does the dying man make his bequest?" He said that the people are to be gathered when death comes to him, and he bears witness and makes his bequest; and he spoke of this at length.

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, prayers of God be upon him, said: "The bequest is a duty upon every Muslim." And Jafar ibn Muhammad, prayers of God be upon him, said: "The bequest is obligatory upon every Muslim, and it does not befit anyone to pass two nights except that his will is written. No dying person dies except that God Almighty restores to him his reason, his hearing, and his sight before death so that he may make his bequest, whether he takes that opportunity or leaves it."

We have narrated from the Imams of the House of the Messenger of God that they permitted a bequest of up to one-third, and no more, of what the testator leaves behind, and they did not allow anything beyond the third except with the consent of the heirs.

Whoever makes a set of bequests in which he directs that the Hajj be performed on his behalf, that a slave be freed, and that expiation be made for his oaths: if he had not performed the Hajj and is unable to, and the bequest falls short of the third, then one begins with the Hajj, then the expiation, then the manumission, and whatever falls short is met from what remains. This is when he has framed the bequest by saying, "Let my third be brought out and spent on such-and-such." But if he made a bequest without naming a third or anything else, and directed that the Hajj be performed for him when he had not performed it, then the Hajj is brought out from the whole of what he left. Likewise, if he states that he owes zakat or any other obligation and directs that it be discharged on his behalf, it is brought out from the entire estate, while whatever is voluntary is brought out from the third. So if he had already performed the Hajj and then directs that a Hajj be performed for him, that is voluntary and is brought out only from the third.

There is no bequest for an heir unless the other heirs permit it, for God Almighty has fixed the heirs inheritance and nothing is added to it, unless the testator makes a bequest for a parent or a relative who does not inherit from him, as when his parents are enslaved or polytheists, or related to him through nursing, or are foster parents. If a man, during the illness in which he dies, acknowledges a debt before his heirs or one of them, his case is examined: if he is suspected, his acknowledgment is not accepted except by clear proof testifying to the origin of what he acknowledged, unless the rest of the heirs permit it; but if he is sick yet upright and trustworthy, his acknowledgment is accepted. When a man has made his bequest, he may revoke it, and he may add to or subtract from his bequest so long as he is alive and understands what he bequeaths. And if he makes bequests exceeding the third, and his heirs come to know of this in his lifetime and approve and allow it to him, then they have no right to retract it after his death.

### On the Obligatory Shares of Inheritance

This concerns the shares of the child, the parents, the spouses, the grandfather, the grandmother, and the brothers.

God, mighty and majestic, has said: ﴿يُوصِيكُمُ اللَّهُ فِي أَوْلَادِكُمْ لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ فَإِنْ كُنَّ نِسَاءً فَوْقَ اثْنَتَيْنِ فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثَا مَا تَرَكَ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ وَاحِدَةً فَلَهَا النِّصْفُ وَلِأَبَوَيْهِ لِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا السُّدُسُ مِمَّا تَرَكَ إِنْ كَانَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وَلَدٌ وَوَرِثَهُ أَبَوَاهُ فَلِأُمِّهِ الثُّلُثُ فَإِنْ كَانَ لَهُ إِخْوَةٌ فَلِأُمِّهِ السُّدُسُ مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِي بِهَا أَوْ دَيْنٍ﴾ — "God charges you concerning your children: to the male the like of the share of two females. If they are women, more than two, theirs is two-thirds of what he left; and if there is only one, hers is the half. To each of his parents a sixth of what he left, if he has a child; but if he has no child and his parents inherit from him, then to his mother a third; and if he has brothers, then to his mother a sixth, after any bequest he makes or any debt." (Al-Nisa: 11)

We have narrated from the People of the House, prayers of God be upon them, that whoever dies leaving children, male and female, with no heir besides them, his inheritance is divided among them so that the male among them receives the like of the share of two females. So too if he leaves a single son and a single daughter, the son receives two-thirds and the daughter one-third. If he leaves a single son with no other heir, the whole inheritance is his. If he leaves two sons, or a number of sons, the inheritance is divided among them equally.

> وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدُ وَهَاجَرُوا۟ وَجَهَدُوا۟ مَعَكُمْ فَأُو۟لَٓئِكَ مِنكُمْ ۚ وَأُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِبَعْضٍۢ فِى كِتَبِ ٱللَّهِ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌۢ

If he leaves a single daughter with no other heir, she takes the half by the share God Almighty has named for her in what we have recited, and the other half is returned to her by the tie of kinship, in accordance with the word of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْ بَعْدُ وَهَاجَرُوا وَجَاهَدُوا مَعَكُمْ فَأُولَئِكَ مِنْكُمْ وَأُولُو الْأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَى بِبَعْضٍ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ — "And those who believed afterward and emigrated and struggled along with you, they are of you; and those who are bound by blood are nearer to one another in the Book of God. Truly God has knowledge of all things." (Al-Anfal: 75) And if they are two daughters, or a group of daughters, the two-thirds is theirs, divided among them equally by the named share, and the remaining third is returned to them by the tie of kinship.

When the children are present together with those entitled to fixed shares, such as the husband, the wife, the grandmother, and the parents, these receive their fixed shares which God Almighty has named for them, and what remains goes to the child or the children, if they are a group, as we have described. If there is no child but there is a child's child, they stand in the place of the child, the males among them as the males and the females as the females, even if they descend and become remote, so long as there is none nearer to the deceased among them; for whoever is nearer of them screens out whoever is more remote. And everyone for whom God Almighty has named a share in the Book among the heirs has a better right than the one He has not named. So when something is left over beyond what He named for him, it is returned to him, and to the sons and the group, if they are of them, in proportion to their inheritance, except for the husband and the wife: nothing is returned to those two unless they have a kinship that entitles them to the return.

An example: a man dies and leaves his two parents and a daughter. The parents take the two sixths, and the daughter takes the half by her named share, and a sixth remains, which is returned to them in proportion to their shares. This is because one share remains out of six, since the two sixths went to the parents, which are two shares, and the half went to the daughter, which is three sixths, making five shares, with one share remaining. That remaining share must likewise be divided over the five, so the estate reverts to five: three-fifths of the inheritance to the daughter and two-fifths to the parents.
